"If you want details you'll have to accept my invitations one of these days. I tend to have a looser tongue during pillow talk."
"Don't take this the wrong way, but I'm really damn curious as to why you haven't been kicked in the balls more than once on this moon."
That seems to quickly sour Neferu's mood.
"Because, Brunis, video recording devices are a luxury on Adastra."
"So you have been? Good, you deserved it."
The wolverine turns to look at me.
"I still don't think this is your fault, but maybe you can tell me what happened so we're not all wasting our breath?"
At this point, Neferu steps in.
"Someone attempted to attack us, likely from one of the separatist groups. It's under investigation."
"The immediate situation was taken care of, but Amicus is taking extra precautions to make sure we are unharmed until we depart for Khemia."
"An attack? What like, they threw crap at you sort of attack, or tried to kill you sort of attack?"
"The latter, but I will tell you the details later. For now, just enjoy the rare opportunity of being able to reside in the grand Adastran Imperial Palace."
"Wha-"
Brunis seems to take Neferu's hint and manages to stifle the reaction that would have followed.

"Well, as long as the two of you are okay. Honestly, this place gives me the creeps. I've only seen footage of this place when Cato tried to murder you. That and the fact they've only got drones around here."
"But I'm especially on edge 'cuz all my stuff got spirited away on a bunch of drones to who-the-hell-knows-where and my medicine went with it. I haven't been able to refill for a whole day now."
The big wolverine manipulates the pipe in his mouth, the one that emanates the herbal smell I recognize him for, before he sucks on it comically hard, his cheeks hollowing out.
I clear my throat.
"Er... Com?"
There's a momentary pause during which both Neferu and Brunis look at me, and I wonder if I've made a fool of myself trying to communicate with the imperial computer while outside.
Thankfully, though--
"Yes, Scipio?"
"Can you locate Brunis's belongings? You were flying them in by drone."
"They have been deposited on the roof."
"What?"
"I have information regarding the situation that may be of note: Brunis's luggage contained an illegal preparation of the Khemian plant {i}papywei{/i} to be vaporized in a pipe contraption."
"Wha--"
"It was properly disposed of via incineration and a report has been filed and sent to Amicus suggesting a 100-year prison sentence for Brunis."
"WHAT?"
Neferu talks over the angry growls coming from the wolverine.
"Why was it dropped on the roof, Com?"
"To follow cargo-loading protocol. All members of the Khemian envoy have had their personal belongings moved to the roof."
"Cargo loading?"
"We are not leaving here until I get my damn {i}pap{/i}! I would rather rip off my one arm than have to go through the stretch without my medicine!"
"Just a moment, does that mean the ship...{i}the{/i} ship has arrived?"
I'm answered by someone I didn't even know is in the gardens with us.
"{i}It's heeeeeere!{/i}"
I know it's Veteris, having heard his over-excitement before, but his normally reedy voice is especially high and harsh now.
We all look around in confusion, and then--
"Holy shit! where'd you come fr--"
"The ship has entered the atmosphere!"
Veteris's manic demeanor seems to disturb my two friends, which is understandable considering they've never seen him in such a state.
It even surprises me a bit, but it's understandable considering this is the beginning of he and I seeing large, state-funded Khemian tech in person for the first time.
"How far away is the ship, Com?"
"Arrival in approximately two minutes and thirty-two seconds."
"Scipio!"
I'm a bit distracted, trying to think of anything else I might need to do here on Adastra before I depart for at least several months.
Longer if all goes well.
I've already gone over my checklist more times than I can count, but I always feel as if I'm missing something.
Veteris is adamant on getting my attention though, leaping in front of me.
"Scipio, my boy!"
His voice has transitioned to a hoarse whisper.
"Remember this moment! Cherish this moment!"
Then he yanks me down to a kneeling position before grabbing my head rather roughly and tilting it toward the sky.
"Behold, your first view of Khemian tech. Let it inspire you, Scipio. It is what Adastra can be!"
For some reason, as the ship arrives, I'm not fully struck by its significance.
It descends in a quiet, controlled manner, as the sun gleams off the metal, and I think at first that maybe they just sent a Parental-built one instead.
It doesn't seem too different from Adastran ships gifted to us by the Romanus parents.
It's a bit more smooth in its architecture, and it's definitely larger than any I'd seen before.
But it's simply that; a different version of what I had seen in the past.
However, as we wait on the roof during takeoff preparations, I finally realize what I'm seeing.
This isn't Parental tech, this actually {i}is{/i} Khemian tech.
I'm not sure what I had been expecting, likely something loud, and powerful, like the Omorfan ships I've seen.
And unlike the many Adastran ships that fly through the air above the capital, it was not simply gifted by the Parents.
This was built by the Khemians themselves.
By engineers that were not only knowledgeable in how to fix ship components when they wore out or malfunctioned, but also in how to actually build them.
And when taking that into consideration, it is certainly impressive... More than that, it's almost inconceivable.
I've known this to be the case since studying Khemian history and culture, but to not be able to tell the difference between their own technology and the Parents is stunning.
It even frightens me a bit as I climb aboard the sibling-built craft as it appears more comfortable, and perhaps even more stable than machinery built by the parents.
This sense of awe and reverence comes to an abrupt end however, as we board the ship and walk through the corridor, just when I happen to peer out the window.
I'm looking out over the lake, a pleasant view, before the palace, well, before {i}everything{/i} flies away.
It happens so fast that I go from seeing the imperial gardens to seeing what I realize is the entirety of the moon, over the course of just a few seconds.
The suddenness of it all, and the odd sensation of seeing such a movement, yet feeling none of it, makes my stomach turn.
My body leans forward, balance teetering as if wanting to fall out the window, and I force myself upright before the others might notice.
Luckily, Amicus and Veteris are looking out the window instead, seemingly unbothered by the sight.
My sudden lurch gets the attention of who is behind me though, and Neferu gently holds onto my elbow.
"Are you alright?"
There usually aren't windows on the few transport ships I've been on in the past, but now that I can see...
It's almost like when I would go sailing with friends on the ocean, the terrible, all-consuming seasickness that came with it.
This is all at once, though.
"Fine... I'm fine."
"You don't look fine."
The big wolverine sidles up next to Neferu, looking at me closely which makes me draw back.
Then the stars bend in the most queasy way imaginable and I stumble to the side again.
I hear my pulse begin to thud dully in my ears, panicking at the way I seem to be losing control of my body, at the same time fearing I might lose control of my stomach as well.
"You are most certainly not fine. Is this your first time in the stretch?"
"Well of course it is, Nef. The hell do you think--"
Neferu is moving me away from the window, but I'm already looking away, horrified.
I'm going to vomit... in front of everyone.
Somehow, Amicus and Veteris have continued on their way, deep in conversation that I vaguely realize I should be making myself a part of.
But that will have to wait.
"I'm fine! Just wondering where a lavatory might be!"
My voice is slightly louder than it should be, though Amicus's deep, resonant voice seems to cover it up, because I can hear him rumbling on as Neferu guides me down another corridor of the ship.
"Hm, we're moving rather fast. I can barely distinguish the stars."
"Of course! The Khemians developed a drive better than the one the Parents lend us!"
"How is this possible?"
Amicus echoes my own thoughts that would be at the forefront of my mind if not for the situation I'm in.
I allow myself to be pushed along until we reach a door that opens automatically without any panels being touched.
"This area is the living quarters. I'm not sure where you'll be bunking, but we'll be sharing the toilet."
We move toward an even smaller door, one that does require the push of a panel.
"Considering the journey is only about 12 hours, it should be somewhat tolerable, I think."
"Do you need anti-nausea medication?"
Too late for that.
"They kick in within minutes."
Still too late.
Neferu makes as if to follow me into the lavatory, probably wanting to help like last time, but I hold up a paw.
"I'm fine! Just..."
My stomach heaves and I fear its contents are about to spew on Neferu.
"I'll be right back!"
I quickly move into the little room, leaving a perturbed Neferu behind as I furiously stab at the panel inside the lavatory until the door slides shut.
I stand over the toilet for several seconds, vaguely thinking to myself that it's quite similar to the ones on Adastra.
I suppose that some things are universal in design, and then what's in my stomach comes out.
I'm in the lavatory for a little while, maybe about 10 minutes, partially to collect myself, but mostly because I'm embarrassed and I just hope Neferu has moved on for now.
Still, at least I had managed not to be sick in the corridor like my stomach wanted to be.
I'm running my paws under the faucet, cleaning myself up before the stream of water suddenly stops and an unfamiliar voice rings in my head.
"Scipio?"
I yelp out loud.
"Apologies. Paw-washing water limit has been reached."
I stand there, staring at my own reflection in the mirror, deciding that what I'd heard came from within my head.
But how?
I begin to panic slightly before I realize that, like with some parental tech I'd interacted with, it must be from my lingua.
So, I respond.
"Erm... Yes? Who is this?"
I get an immediate answer in return.
"I am Ahm, the State-sponsored computer assistant of Khemia."
"Oh... Oh! Yes, I know of you. I've studied..."
I trail off, reminding myself that this is a computer, and it does not care about what I've studied, or about anything at all.
"You have studied me?"
The computer asks in a slightly curious tone after a polite pause.
This is very odd.
It's odd that it's speaking directly into my lingua; Com never did that, and I doubt he can.
But something else is even more strange about this computer that I'm trying to put my finger on.
"Yes, I--I did not expect you to speak through my lingua. It was a bit startling."
I would remember that bit of information if I came across it in my studies.
"Apologies, Scipio. I was converted to lingua use only unless otherwise directed. This is to protect the privacy of all who use my services. Would you prefer auditory communication instead?"
"No, this is fine."
"Very well."
I wonder the same thing that I wondered when I first saw this ship, the same thing Amicus questioned when we entered the stretch.
How is this possible?
It implies that the Khemians have learned how to access and manipulate the lingua directly.
While this is impressive, it also rekindles my unease.
What else might they be able to do if they can fully access the tiny piece of machinery embedded in my brain?
Do we really know the extent of Khemian knowledge and power?
Is it really possible to do such things alone, without Parental help?
As I'm contemplating this, Ahm fills the silence, like a sapient noticing a lull in the conversation.
"I can provide you with non-water methods to sanitize, if you wish. Unfortunately, our water reserves are limited."
"Er, no, no I'm fine. Thank you."
"You are welcome Scipio, and it's a pleasure meeting you."
"You as well..."
I realize what bothers me about him, aside from accessing my neurotech without my consent or foreknowledge.
With Com, I never considered him truly "intelligent".
I never once questioned if he had thoughts or feelings of his own while he communicated.
I could say Com is comparatively stupid, but he's simply a program that consumes information, analyzes, then outputs sentences based on that information.
This Khemian machine is something different, and I wonder how widespread it is on the jackal planet.
The eerie atmosphere persists as I stare into the mirror, thinking about how something here isn't right.
I banish the thought for now and adjust my robes, trying to keep my emotions under control.
Now is not the time.
I can discuss it with Veteris, or maybe even Amicus later.
With that in mind, I look into the mirror one last time to assess the state of my facial fur before tapping the panel and stepping out into the corridor.
"Oh!"
Why is he still here?
It has to have been at least fifteen minutes.
"Ah! Er, hello..."
I had jumped just like Neferu, and now I quickly smooth down my robe, a gesture meant to cover up my reaction, but one that only makes it all the more obvious.
Had he been trying to listen through the door?
Either way, it puts me on guard.
"Hello..."
I pause, trying to think of something to say, but I can't think of anything, so I simply ask what would be most normal in this situation.
"Did you need the lavatory?"
"No, just checking to see if you are well. You looked quite shaken up."
As Neferu confirms the reason I thought he might be lingering here, I can't help just a small flash of irritation.
He's looking after me, which is kind and generous of him, as he has no obligation to do so.
But it certainly makes me appear childish, him looking after me this closely.
Perhaps even suspicious.
I adjust my expression to appear more serious, but also calm.
A cool, emotionless look.
"I am fine, thank you, Neferu. Please, do not worry so much for my well-being. I do not wish to be the reason for you neglecting your own duties."
The look on Neferu's face is hard to describe.
It's not a pleasant look, and it's enough to throw me off despite him not saying anything.
Another moment of silence passes, and I begin to think over Khemian etiquette, wondering if I violated a taboo of some kind.
Of course, Neferu would be understanding of such things, but considering that we are not on Adastra anymore, perhaps he is less forgiving now.
Just as I begin to open my own mouth to ask what the issue is, Neferu finally speaks.
"I see. Very well. I shall leave you to attend to your own matters, then. Apologies for bruising your wolven pride."
Neferu turns on his heel before briskly walking away.
I stand there alone, the low hum of the ship's various moving parts the only sound filling the heavy silence while I try to understand what just happened.
I had acted within diplomatic norms.
Really any interaction among diplomats is normal as long as only words are used, specifically the right words.
Present an aura of civility, even if your primal instincts are telling you to knock the other's teeth out.
This was one of the main issues of pre-Drusus Adastra.
Apparently wolven "diplomats" of the era routinely took swings at other Siblings, and even amongst themselves when they became angry, or offended.
Despite this being over 10,000 years in the past, it is a reputation that still haunts us.
I suppose it is not helpful that our experimental attempts at a republic have resulted in brawls within the senate in just the past year.

I'm sure footage of the fights was shown gleefully across the news channels of the other Siblings, showing that we haven't changed, that there's something innately wrong with our culture or even our species.
While I might admit that wolven hubris has been the main hindrance throughout our history, I'm not going to allow myself to be treated as some sort of idiot savage.
We have our own culture, our own language, our own universities--
"{i}We witnessed it... We saw you bleed because of him... Perhaps he wishes to see you bleed even more?{/i}"
--and despite my admiration for Khemia as a whole, they have their own issues with hubris.
Neferu is a clear example of that.
"{i}Wolven pride...{/i}"
The hackles along my shoulders begin to rise, and I work to contain myself.
What an odd and frankly childish thing for him to say.
I suppose it was insensitive of me to act in such a manner toward someone who so recently called me a friend, but his reaction was clearly hostile... and hypocritical.
I suspect that he has issues deeper than his facade will ever admit.
But the unfamiliar anger in my mind dampens as I remember my duties.
Not even one hour into my mission and I'm already failing.
I stand there for a while in silence, wavering as if on the edge of a cliff before gritting my teeth and clenching my paws into fists.
No, none of this.
Either I will succeed, or I will fail, but in both cases I will continue on and serve the empire, all for the greater good of Adastra.
I am not some wolven bitch for Khemians to look down upon and shake their heads at.
So, pushing through the hurt and embarrassment and blinking past the blur of moisture in my eyes, I set off aimlessly, unsure of where to go, but just wanting to move.
I'm sure they'll summon me through Ahm if I'm needed.
As I walk quickly through the corridor, I happen to glance out the windows, having forgotten about the nauseatingly bending light, and my stomach lurches instantly.
But I'm still motivated by my sudden burst of furious confidence in myself, so I say in a low, stern voice;
"No."
I force myself to continue looking while I walk, demanding my stomach to settle.
Still, it doesn't appear that I have gained voluntary control over the mechanisms that dictate nausea in my body.
Already irritated by my early failure, I force myself to continue staring.
This is punishment for being unable to handle simple, easy things that no one else has difficulty handling.
It's similar to when I struggled with insomnia when I was first away from home at university.
It had been disturbingly satisfying to tell my own body that it only had itself to blame for being so tired during lectures, and that maybe it should sleep next time.
I do the same now, mentally sneering at my roiling stomach for being so weak that it can't handle the movement of light.
Neferu's assurances that others have a weak mind like my own is difficult to believe now.
He probably only says whatever he thinks I want--
My meandering thoughts are brought to a very sudden and rude end as my feet catch something on the floor and my paws flail out for something to grab.
I yelp loudly as a few toe claws bend back before landing heavily on my side, my paw pads slapping the smooth, hard floor to keep from falling further.
Rubbing at the left side of my hip, I look down at my feet in confusion.
Three metallic crates stick out from a doorway into the corridor, and my foot had caught the corner of the one sticking out furthest.
"Huh?"
There's a heavy grunt that I recognize immediately and Brunis sticks his head around the doorway with a stern squint before looking down and seeing me.
"Skip? What the hell are you doing?"
My irritation and self-pity are only amplified now.
I get to my feet roughly, likely flashing Brunis with my undergarments as I don't bother trying to keep my robe down.
He's the type not to care anyway.
"Is leaving your belongings out for others to injure themselves on a normal Khemian custom?"
Brunis blinks at me, probably due to the fact that he's never seen me act like this.
"Huh? I'm moving stuff in right now. Is it a wolf thing to not look where you're going?"
"I'm simply curious as to whether or not I should be more careful around you Khemians especially if I want to return to Adastra in one piece."
"What in the hell crawled up your ass, Skip?"
I have to admit that Brunis's techniques for de-escalating tense situations, despite seeming informal and unrefined, are disarming.
I sigh and massage the bridge of my snout with both paws, my stomach lurching again, exacerbated by the rough fall.
"I don't know, Brunis. Ahm? Could I get an anti-emetic, please?"
"Certainly, a drone has been dispatched to your location."
"Speaking of which, I {i}just{/i} had to deal with Neferu biting my head off for being fat."
I turn my attention back to Brunis.
"'Speaking of which'? What do you mean by that?"
"Uh... Oh, speaking of things up your--aw crap."
Brunis winces.
"You guys are kinda uptight about that sort of thing, aren't ya? I didn't mean it like that, you could have been up his ass for all I--"
I wave my paw, providing an escape for the flustered wolverine.
The anger I had felt already beginning to dissipate.
It's difficult to be mad at Brunis anyway.
"Yes, 'uptight'. Anyway, I am sorry that I snapped at you. I am not feeling well."
"Yeah, looks like you ain't."
Brunis watches as I am suddenly distracted by a smooth, glossy black dome that levitates toward me, then extends a tiny, white wafer.
I take it with some confusion.
"Um, thanks. Do I need water, or..."
"Goes under the tongue."

I try not to visibly blanch at the idea of letting vile medication sit in my mouth for any amount of time, but quick relief is preferable, assuming it works as quickly as Neferu said, or if it even works after the nausea has set in.
"Alright. Anyway, what were you saying about Neferu being upset? Does he usually criticize your size?"
I carefully drop the square wafer under my tongue, hardly feeling it land before I close my mouth, and it dissolves instantly.
Brunis shrugs.
"Not really. I was in the hall bringing stuff in and he told me to move and not take up the entire space, or something."
"He scurried off before I could ask what crawled up {i}his{/i} ass. You two fighting, or something?"
Brunis looks at me, waiting for a response.
I point at my mouth to remind him of the medication while being simultaneously glad to have an excuse not to respond.
"Oh, you can swallow it now. It's made with some weird nanotech stuff that makes ya absorb it in like, a few seconds."
Though Brunis doesn't sound like he knows what he's talking about, he's definitely right;
The nausea is almost instantly gone, and I'm glad for this Khemian {i}nanotech{/i}.
I expect the taste to be bitter and acrid, but instead it's slightly sweet, almost nonexistent.
"Fascinating."
I say it to myself, never having had an anti-emetic that worked after the fact, though Brunis responds with a face of disgust.
"I'd rather feel sick than take that shit. Makes me feel slow as hell all day. {i}Pap{/i} takes care of motion sickness and all my other problems, too."
The wolverine looks down at the large crates.
"By the way, you're rooming with me. I already pushed your stuff in."
I take a look around Brunis to peer inside at a small room with two beds on either side, one of which already has two identical metal crates next to it.
"Oh, thank you, Brunis."
It makes me feel guilty, knowing that he had hauled my belongings in first, only for me to yell at him.
"Sure. Don't know why they dropped all our shit here instead of in the actual room, though. Yo, Ahm!"
It's silent for a moment, and I wonder if Brunis failed to summon the assistant, but then I remember how it works.
"Get me some {i}pap{/i}! They destroyed my stash on Adastra."
Brunis gives me a knowing look.
"Probably 'destroyed' by that asshole magistrate. I'll bet he's high off his ass right now--"
"For the sake of Ahhotep!"
I'm confused by the sudden change in tone, then I realize he's responding to something Ahm said.
I suppose there are downsides to having a computer assistant only you can hear.
"You want me to list everything? Headache, Backache, stomachache, heartache... Yeah, great, thanks."
Brunis turns his attention back to me as I look down at one of the crates.
Normally, it would be levitating slightly off the ground through the use of magnets, though I suppose the floor here is not compatible.
"Here, I will push these ones inside. It sounds like you are in a great deal of pain."
Brunis shrugs.
"Eh, I'll live. You just gotta give Ahm enough reasons to justify dealing it out. I don't mind you helping, though."
I grunt as I slide one of the cases across the floor, wishing that it at least had wheels.
"Isn't drug-usage free and plentiful on Khemia?"
Brunis makes a snorting sound.
"That what they tell ya in wolf school?"
His knowing, condescending tone might have irritated me, but I know Brunis doesn't mean for it to demean or hurt me.
Unlike what Neferu just did.
Besides, snide remarks about wolves are something I will probably hear regularly on Khemia, so this is a good opportunity to practice separating my emotions and my work.
"Well, not told, but shown footage of addicted Khemians in the streets of the capital."
"Ugh, propaganda."
"Is it not true, though?"
"Doesn't matter if it's true. What matters is what they're using it for."
I decide to let the topic go at that point, knowing that there's truth in what we both said.
Also because it's difficult to continue talking under the strain of pushing the crate.
Brunis gives a much louder grunt as he follows me into the room, pushing the last crate.
"Anyway, it does seem that you are in a lot of pain."
I come to a stop at the foot of what I assume is Brunis's bed while the wolverine follows shortly after.
"Whew! One sec..."
He stoops to catch his breath.
"If the aches flare up real bad, I just get a script from the palace doctor."
My slightly heavy breathing is dwarfed by the huffing and panting of the wolverine as he leans heavily against the crate.
"I don't like 'em very much because not being able to feel pain is kinda scary to me. But like I said, it ain't bad. I can still walk."
Brunis sits on the crate, his sizable rear covering most of it.
"Is it related to when you were injured?"
"Yup! Happened when I was real young though, so it feels normal to me."
I wonder if he's going to tell me what happened, but when he doesn't, I don't press further.
"Anyway {i}pap{/i} helps a bit with that, but it's mostly mental shit where it really does wonders for me. Keeps me sane, I think."
"Oh? How so?"
I try not to seem too interested.
Even though we aren't on Adastra, the idea of a psychoactive drug so readily available is... frightening.
"Well... I guess it kinda makes everything make a little more sense, slows stuff down so I can think through it properly."
That sounds rather nice.
"And what I like most about it is that it makes experiencing emotions more... more meaningful, I guess?"
"I dunno though! Never had to explain it before. Just feels good."
I raise my brow.
"Doesn't that get in the way of your work?"
I know he smokes the pipe almost constantly, and while I can understand using it for leisure, I would be hesitant to alter my mind while doing important work on behalf of the Parents.
"Well, that's the thing. Things seem more connected and it's easier to empathize. That's important for diplomacy."
I think, wanting to inquire more about emotions and diplomacy, but I'm also unsure if I should be discussing such matters with Brunis.
Despite his outward demeanor, I know that he's a highly skilled and experienced negotiator in Khemian politics.
I have to remember they're watching and observing too, and even if I am the lowest ranking Adastran here, that could make me a target.
I'm spared making the decision as a soundless drone floats into the cabin, this time extending a small, black capsule, about the size of my thumb.
Brunis eyes it before plucking the capsule rather aggressively from the drone.
"Thanks, this'll last me a solid half-hour, Ahm. Anyway, yeah--"
Brunis uses a flicking motion with his thumb to open the tiny capsule.
"--you shouldn't let personal issues get in the way, but it's important to empathize with the side you're negotiating with."
I watch him pack the strange pipe contraption for a while, the wolverine handling the flakey green concoction carefully so as not to spill any of it.
"Can it help with... distracting thoughts?"
I can't stop myself from asking.
I have, for the most part, been able to keep myself in check for the better part of two years.
But the past hour has left me wondering if it's all about to fall apart.
I realize then, how desperate I am for some kind of solution, a fix for this dysfunctional brain of mine.
I suppose my approach isn't subtle, however.
Brunis leans back and eyes me closely, his pipe held in one paw.
"It might. It's different for everyone, but I know people that use it to focus... You doing okay, by the way?"
"Definitely! As you know, it's very illegal to possess such substances on Adastra, so I am simply curious about this part of Khemian culture."
Brunis continues to study me, and I try to keep my paws from fidgeting by clasping them together.
Perhaps it does not matter, considering Neferu will likely tell Brunis about my issues anyway, despite his promise.
"Well, {i}pap{/i} is just the Khemian strain of {i}chronoma{/i}, which is native to Omorfa."
"Kinda funny that it's banned on Adastra when you guys {i}borrowed{/i} so much from the cats, haha!"
Brunis winks at me to lighten the jab, even though I'm too anxious at the idea of this plant to even really register it.
"Anyway, if you really are interested, I can take you to an Omorfan dispensary."
"The cats {i}really{/i} know their shit when it comes to anything plant-related, obviously. They got a bunch of stuff that might be better for you."
"Ah, well, maybe I'll have a look at one sometime."
Brunis can clearly see that I am interested, which only convinces me to back out of this odd, reckless attempt to fix myself.
While I know that much of the education I received on the use of recreational drugs was simply state-sponsored propaganda, I'm still deeply uneasy about it.
Using a drug to patch over a mental deficiency like mine simply seems... unwise.
Just as I'm about to head over to my side of the room, however, Brunis sticks his pipe out toward me.
"Wanna puff? I know it's not a wolf thing, but it'd be rude of me not to offer."
I stare at the pipe for a second, my curiosity rekindled for just a moment, before the words of my instructor in mindfulness comes to me.
{i}Meditation is key, Scipio. Alcohol only damages your self-awareness and self-control.{/i}.
I assume he would say this about most drugs, especially those used for mind-alteration.
So I hold up a paw.
"I am tempted due to wanting to understand Khemian culture better, but I should avoid any psychoactive substances while I'm on this mission."
"That's probably a good idea. It can be a hard one to predict if you've never had it."
The big wolverine ambles over to his own bed, sitting down with a heavy sigh, inhaling from his pipe, the room filling with that herbal smell before it quickly dissipates again.
It must be the air filtration system vacuuming it away.
"So... what do wolves do for fun in a place where everything's illegal?"
I sit back, a bit more sluggish now, probably due to the nausea medication.
"We have alcohol."
Saying this reminds me of the time I asked my doctor for something to help cope with the anxiety three years ago.
I especially remember his look of surprise and confusion before telling me that sedatives were a womanly medication and that I should instead go buy some cheap drink instead.
It certainly felt manly, boldly drinking an entire mug of toxic-tasting ale while my friends cheered me on.
And it did help, at least until I began blacking out from drinking too much, and that frightened me away from it.
Probably for the best.
Brunis makes a face.
"Blegh, not a fan of the stuff. Makes me sick and gives me a headache."
"I don't enjoy it anymore. I mainly partook to better match the mood of my friends on our nights off."
"Oh, I get that, AND it tastes like shit! Sure, 'acquired tastes' and all, but it all tastes the same to me, just different shades of shit."
"Yes, the taste would probably make me vomit these days, but mostly, I didn't like having less control over myself. I've seen a few friends completely consumed by it, and it's a terrible thing."
I wonder about one of them now, Gaius, who had gone from perfect marks and attendance at university, to living on the streets.
It had happened after he lost his best friend in the riots, who had also been a friend of mine.
{i}Spurius.{/i}
My breath hitches and I sit up straighter.
"Sorry, Brunis, but do you mind if I meditate?"
"Oh yeah, not at all. Do you, uh, need me to leave?"
"No, you're fine."
Brunis nods and lies back on his bed, staring at the ceiling as he continues to smoke his pipe.
I sit cross-legged at the foot of my bed, beginning with the familiar first step of focusing on my breathing.
I listen to my breathing and pay close attention to the rise and fall of my chest and shoulders.
I smell the {i}papywei{/i} along with the slightly stale and metallic scent of the recycled air.
My mind is surprisingly flexible right now, as if I could try more complex meditation without issue, but I don't dare do that without my instructor.
Maybe Neferu might know how--
My breathing suddenly quickens, and I immediately refocus my thoughts.
I'm here, in the moment, without judgement, imagining myself to have the transparency of a window--
"{i}Because they're mindless, uneducated scum. What else should we expect from those districts?{/i}"
Breathing, remember breathing.
But my mind seems to want to leave, almost like it's levitating, being drawn toward something above.
My eyes fly open, shocked.
"Shit, sorry. Tried to lift one of the crates on my bed so I didn't have to bend over and I dropped--"
"Skip?"
I can't move, or speak.
Everything appears strange, vivid and crisp.
I'm trembling and I feel my already-tense muscle tensing tighter, somehow.
I can smell the assassin's blood and entrails again.
"{i}The{/i} {i}ahewawi{/i} {i}is going to stay with you forever, isn't it?{/i}"
A voice I've only heard in my dreams whispers directly into my ear.
It's a real voice, not one that comes from my head, or imagination.
It's a rustling of dead leaves, rattling out of the throat of something ancient, something that knows me better than I know myself.
I'm back in the den, so I reach for the only escape I can, the magnetic force that was pulling at my mind earlier.
"Shit!"
I hear Brunis's panicked voice, but I'm far too detached to even wonder about what he said, or why.
A distant jolt through my head and body, but that's it.
Then I feel nothing.
"{i}This is what true peace is like, Scipio, but death is even better, because you don't exist at all.{/i}"
"{i}Imagine a universe without life. How peaceful things would be then.{/i}"
Nothing.
{i}It's the only perfect state that can be achieved.{/i}.
"{i}Sapients, you or anyone else, cannot be trusted. Remember how the cretin wolves treated you? Remember how the Khemians treat the wolves? Remember how Neferu treats you?{/i}"
"{i}And do you remember your true purpose here, how you are treating Neferu?{/i}"
I hate it.
"{i}More importantly, remember how the Parents treat sapients, in the name of 'agency', and yet what choice do any of you have?{/i}"
"{i}You can help those like you, and by extension, all other sapients.{/i}"
I would if I could.
"{i}You can.{/i}"
I have no idea how long it's been, but when I'm back in my own mind, I'm even more confused about where I am.
I wonder if I have died.
Like Urbicus died.
Maybe I fell and hit my head, like Spurius died.
Or maybe our ship somehow crashed, and I've been left to float through space forever.
Or at least a few more seconds before I suffocate.
That would be alright, I decide, even as I take a deep, easy breath of air.
I would rather exist this way; insignificant and meaningless against the monolithic emptiness of the universe.
It's all strangely... peaceful.
"My goodness, Scipio. If only your friends and colleagues could hear half of what you think."
A deep, but feminine voice comes from seemingly every direction.
The fur raises on the nape of my neck and I try to look around, to find the source of the voice.
"What? Those weren't my thoughts, though."
There's a deep, raspy chuckle, one that I recognize as distinctly feline, the type I've heard from recordings that involved Hindo tigers.
"Perhaps not, but do you not agree with them, young wolf?"
"Who are you? Are you from Hindo?"
"Very good, especially for a wolf living in a time where Hindo has severed relations with Adastra completely."
"But can you guess who I actually am?"
Her eyes are so piercing, so intense that although I want to ask again what exactly is happening, I feel obliged to answer.
And so, I quickly run through a list of tigresses I know of, only one of which is alive; the current ruler of Hindo.
"Er, Maharani Arti?"
The tigress eyes me closely so that I lower my ears, just wishing that I can go back soon.
"Consider the impossibility of where you are. You think Arti would try to come all the way here to talk to some rebellious pup?"
I swallow hard, trying to keep my breathing even, because whatever this is, I think that it is somehow real.
But there could be an explanation.
"Are... are you Meera?"
The quiet smile on her face answers my question.
"Well, I suppose two attempts is not terrible, though I must say that the human knew immediately."
"A--Amicus's human?"
"Yes."
The voice of dead leaves is gone now, as is the feeling of nothingness, and I'm embarrassed as I long to be back there, knowing the tigress knows what I'm thinking.
Meera stays silent, though the look on her face tells me that she's waiting for me to speak.
"Did the... are the Parents doing this? Are they making contact with me?"
It is rumored that they did the same with the human.
Meera is quiet for a while, so I stay quiet as well, unable to think of any other reason for this to be happening if it really {i}is{/i} happening.
"The parents are a complex matter, Scipio. Direct communication with them is impossible, unless they break their own rules against interference."
She narrows her eyes.
"Think more logically though. Concerning the voice, would the parents say such things to you?"
I answer honestly.
"I don't know."
I try to think logically, as she told me to do.
"Maybe it's a test? Or maybe this is part of the plan? Do you know who that was? Was it you?"
Meera is quiet again, but it's more like she's pondering something.
"I cannot say for certain, Scipio, but what I do know is that you don't trust the Parents."
That sends a jolt of fear through me.
"I do! I just don't understand what the purpose of any of this is."
That tiger chuckle again.
"Take comfort in the fact that it's no fault of your own. The Parents plant all the seeds, after all."
"Why did you bring me here? Is there something that I am supposed to do, or maybe you have instructions?"

"You brought yourself here, Scipio. The stretch drive makes the layers between planes more permeable. Would you believe that the Parents physically stopped the human from killing Amicus while they were in the stretch?"
I don't know if I do, and I don't know what to say.
"Such agency they've gifted us with, eh?"
Meera taps a finger to her head.
The fear continues to rise in me, not wanting to anger the Parents, and not wanting to be dead, because the Amalgamation is where we truly go.
"You fear death, you fear the Amalgamation. Rather, you believe it is an abomination, and deep down, though you will not admit it even to yourself..."
My fur bristles and I try to jolt myself awake, but nothing happens.
"...You do not trust the Parents, or anyone for that matter."
Am I going to be punished?
They know I'm a fraud, on a mission to further Parental agendas when I don't believe them to be right.
I'm only here for selfish reasons.
"I believe disagreeing with their 'grand plan' is one of the lesser troubling thoughts in your head. You have enough hatred to set fire to those wolves yourself."
"You are capable of dark things, Scipio, but who wouldn't be after that day?"
I realize my legs are trembling, but I can at least feel them again, and that gives me hope.
Please wake up.
Meera raises a paw.
"Easy, young wolf. I am only here to help you, to warn, and to advise. You need guidance, and I am here to offer it if you will take it."
I frown and rack my brain for the lessons I had on Meera, if she was ever used in this manner in the past.
Her main purpose was that of self-sacrifice, to push Drusus in the correct direction for the empire.
She has little to do with the Parents.
As far as I know, it is only the Monitors that communicate for the Parents.
Does that mean--

"--that this is not sanctioned by the Parents? Yes. And do not be afraid that you are not in lockstep with their vision for the future. They've limited themselves by professing the importance of free will, choice without interference."
"I am not afraid to admit that I disagree with them completely. I never entered the Amalgamation as I believe that it is an attack on life, rather than a preservation of it."
"Besides, they can't even agree with each other. They bicker just as much as the Siblings."
The borders of this odd, in-between world begin to shimmer and fade, and I realize it's ending.
"Wait! Please, you say that you did not have to go to the Amalgamation? That--that you can help fix me? Can you tell me more of that voice? Please, don't leave me yet!"
Meera smiles at me, at my desperation that I know must look insane, but I truly am desperate.
"This will not be the last time we speak. Trust that I will appear again when the time is right. This was merely an introduction."
"O--Okay... Thank you, Meera."
"It was a pleasure meeting you, Scipio. Until next time."
But in the relief of escape, another voice adds their own thoughts just as I'm leaving, one that I recognize.
Higher-pitched and female.
That of a jackal.
"There we go! Scipio, say this to Neferu; '{i}nettek aum hotep akh{/i}.'"
"Tell him to stop sulking like a spoiled prince and to communicate with you. This is important. He'll understand."
I'm in my body once more, and I'm lying on something soft.
"--I don't know! He said he was gonna meditate and then he looked at me all scared before his eyes just rolled into the back of his head!"
I can't move though, my body locked in place, though my fingers and ears start to regain some movement, twitching as I try to break free.
"Did you give him something?"
"No!"
"Skip?"
My paws begin to shift.
"Hey, look! He's moving."
A touch on my shoulder, gentle and tentative.
"Did you blow the vapor in his direction? He's a wolf and has no experience with that drug. He could be very sensitive to it!"
"If that's all it takes to get him high then why hasn't he ever freaked out when he's sitting next to me?"
"I'm sorry to tell you something you already know, but {i}pap{/i} smells terrible. He turns his nose away whenever you get close!"
As I begin to come back to what I believe is reality, they continue to go back and forth, and I imagine their voices in a sparring match.
It reminds me of the one time Neferu managed to convince the wolverine to spar.
Despite his build and size, Brunis isn't much of a fighter.
The match barely lasted more than a minute before Brunis was on his knees and retching so loud he sounded like a giant, squawking bird.
Even though I felt bad for him at the time, I chuckle, surprising even myself.
They stop arguing.
Then, all at once, the paralysis releases me, and I shift slowly.
I'm confused for a moment, then sit up quickly.
I realize the scene I'm making right now, but I don't know what happened.
All I can do is say the only thing that might confirm I'm not going insane, before I forget it.
"{i}Nettek aum hotep akh.{/i}"

The way they stare at me makes my ears fold back for a moment, embarrassed about my clumsy, heavy accent despite the situation, knowing my words are heard directly by the both of them, unfiltered by their linguas.
But I'm more worried that if it was only a dream, I'd probably spoken some faux-Khemian gibberish pulled from my pre-intermediate knowledge of the language.
I almost want to make the excuse that it takes years to learn Khemian, especially for wolves.
Neferu's reaction says otherwise though, but I'm not sure if it's a preferable one.
"What did you say?"
I stare back at him, feeling out-of-body, as if I've suddenly been dropped here from a distant moon.
Clearly it meant something, possibly something serious, or even something bad.
"I don't know. I was meditating and got lost and... I don't know."
I cover my face, finally overwhelmed and not knowing what to do.
What the hell is happening to me?
It's quiet, but I hear them murmur to each other for a moment, followed by movement, and when I look up, Brunis is gone.
The bed shifts with added weight as Neferu sits next to me.
He's quiet, as if waiting for me to say more, to explain what I had just said.

"I'm sorry, I don't know what that means. I know the word 'peace' and maybe 'welcome', but there's a lack of resources to learn Khemian on Adastra, and it's especially hard for Adastrans because the differences..."
I realize I'm over-explaining and trail off, deciding to wait for Neferu to break the silence.
"It sounded fine, Skip. It's the first time I've heard a wolf speak a full sentence in Khemian, actually. But I'm much more interested in what prompted you to say it."
"Is it a bad thing to say?"
I try to keep my paws from gripping my thighs too tightly, but Neferu shakes his head.
"It means 'Welcome, and be at ease, brother'."
As if to pay me in kind, he says it in Adastran.
Now I hear Neferu's voice unfiltered, but his accent is pleasant, almost sing-song in its quality, and I know it sounds better than my own bumbling accent stumbling over Khemian.
I can tell he's fluent just from that sentence.
Neferu waves a paw as if brushing something aside.
"Roughly, anyway. It can be worded in many ways, but I'm wondering where you heard it, or why you said it."
I look down at the sterile metal floor of the ship, only now able to absorb what I'd seen and heard while I had been meditating, though meditation has never done anything like that to me before.
As I think back on it, I don't want to tell him the majority of what I saw and heard, but I can at least tell him about the third and final voice.
"I heard a voice while meditating, a female jackal, I think."
Neferu is clearly trying to keep his reaction muted, but he can't fully hide his surprise.
I fidget with my tail as it curls around in my lap.
"Should I be wary of it? I didn't see anyone."
"Did that voice say anything else?"
My ears duck down again.
"It mentioned that, erm... You should communicate with me and not to sulk like a... A spoiled prince, or something--"
Neferu makes a soft huffing sound of surprise, almost like a laugh.
"It really is her, then."
"Who?"
"My youngest sister, Aya."
"Really? Why... why would she contact me? How can she even make contact like that? She's on Khemia, right?"

I'd studied the royal family, but there was a noticeable lack of information on the youngest of the four siblings aside from her being some sort of religious scholar who performed traditional Khemian rituals for the family.
"She's on Khemia, yes, but as to how she's contacting you, or why, I'm not sure. She's certainly never contacted me like that in the past three years."
There's a touch of bitterness in his voice, likely covering up his hurt feelings if it's true that Aya is the only member of his family that Neferu has an amicable relationship with.
"But how is it even possible for her to do that? She said you would understand."

"Well, her duties involve things that are quite abstract and beyond my own understanding. If she scolded me and said I should 'communicate' with you, she might have an interest in you specifically, for whatever reason."
It's quiet for a few seconds.
"But how does she even know me? This is making me wonder if I'm still dreaming, Neferu. You don't even seem that surprised that she's able to do this."
I know he's not telling me everything he knows.
Neferu opens his mouth, then closes it, as if struggling to find the right words.
"Don't worry too much about it. She's very... she can be hard to understand and sometimes gets excited over things that others would find insignificant."
I wonder for a moment if I told Neferu she wanted better communication between us, because it's not happening.
"Neferu, you are emotionally close to her, right?"
"Yes. Probably because the two of us didn't exactly fit in with the family, though she's doing a much better job of it now than I am."
"So she must have told you, at some point, what she's capable of, of what her role is? Neferu, she's reaching across light years to speak to me. I'm a bit concerned about that."
Neferu sighs deeply.
"The truth is that I am under Parental oath not to discuss it. I might not even be allowed to say that, but I'll wait for a Monitor to smite me if that's the case."
"I know it all sounds very strange and even frightening, so I didn't want to add to your worries. Keep in mind that she, like I, can be a bit dramatic at times."
"I see..."
I don't see.
I still have many, many questions, about the other voices she seems to be fighting against, but maybe I can talk to Aya herself about it, if I'm even allowed to do so.
"I can say that if she has the ability to astral project to contact other sapients, then that is new information to me, however it's not out of the realm of possibility considering what she does."
"If that were always the case, I would have expected her to have given me advice over the past three years. Again, I might get in trouble for even saying this much."
I think.
"I apologize in advance for even suggesting this, but you have every reason to believe that she's currently alive, right?"
"Of course. Why wouldn't she be?"
Now Neferu is the one looking nervous.
I fully decide then that I won't bring up Meera, who is very much dead.
"Sorry, just trying to figure out how this is happening. I've heard claims that un-amalgamated spirits can do that."

"Well if that were somehow the case, I would be a bit upset that she appeared to you only to tell me to stop feeling sorry for myself. Not entirely bad advice though. However, she would be amalgamated, no doubt."
I can still see that I've worried Neferu, so I decide to move the conversation along by asking about what she meant.
"That makes sense. Maybe I can meet her when we arrive, assuming it really was her?"
"Of course, I'll introduce you."
"Thank you, Neferu. So if you're not allowed to discuss her duties, what do you think she meant when she said to 'communicate' with me?"
"Judging by what you told me, I think she wants me to help you, instead of acting as I did when you came out of the lavatory."
I had almost forgotten about that.
Neferu's sister encouraging us to communicate will be very helpful to me as she seems to have a good deal of influence, and not just over her brother.
"Well, I did react in a rude way myself. I could tell that what I said was hurtful to you. I was just embarrassed about being seen in that moment of weakness."
"Ah, you need not apologize. I was being nosy and you reacted in an understandable way. If you'll accept an excuse, my overreaction is rooted in past experiences."
"Oh, how so?"
"I once knew an Omorfan by the name of Alexios."
"Oh... You knew him, personally?"
Alexios, the Sibling pet and rumored lover of Cassius, the former false emperor and also Amicus's brother.
Alexios was an agent of Omorfa, sent to Adastra to sow chaos in the very fabric of our society, a mission that was ultimately successful.
One could say that he is the main reason for the riots occurring.
"Well, I knew him, but I doubt anyone knew him personally, aside from maybe Cassius. Anyway, despite nearly toppling Adastra, he was never a very good spy, but he was underestimated."
"And he struck Cassius's fancy. It's easier to be a spy when you have a direct connection to the very heart of power."
Neferu looks at me candidly, in case I missed it.
But I didn't, I already know he sees right through me, but I also think I sometimes see right through him.
In all honestly though, I wasn't thinking about the game I, or the both of us, are playing.
I should be calculating the best way to establish a relationship that Neferu will become emotionally reliant upon, even if it's detrimental to Khemia.
Veteris told me earlier that this is an especially promising exploit considering Neferu's family relationship is unmoored, to put it lightly.
That's my end goal, despite the slim odds of it going that far, or even being needed.
His brother and younger sister are both in positions of much higher power and influence, and after learning more about his youngest sister, and her secretive directives, she might be as well.
But for the first time, for right now at least, I'm following my emotions where they take me.
The dutiful part of me, the part that I thought was all of me, is scolding myself, but after the experience I just had, I wonder if it's even the most pressing issue.
It's a bit alarming, but I calm myself by reasoning that this is simply the best way to approach Neferu, that my beliefs and goals have not changed.
One strange experience during meditation, an experience I'm not even sure was real, should not be able to cause that.
Another part of me, one so unfamiliar it makes my skin crawl, knows it was real, but that won't help with staying calm.
"I see."
"Well, whenever he found himself cornered, he often resorted to a very... strange state of mind."
"Basically, he would exhibit the expression and emotion of a rock, a classic, diplomatic, defensive maneuver he often used to get out of situations he couldn't, though he was never subtle about it."

"He is possibly the most selfish, amoral political official I have ever had the displeasure of dealing with. To be clear, I knew his motives were to serve Omorfa, which can be argued to be the most anti-Adastran Sibling world--"
"--but what I didn't expect was a sniveling coward, willing to destroy the foundation of an entire Sibling civilization and cause loss of life in the thousands."
I nod, though having not known the cat, I have few opinions about him aside from the fact that he's an Omorfan.
Omorfa has always loathed Adastra, as they see us to be the biggest threat to stability in the {i}Galaxias{/i}.
They've even gone a step further than Hindo, suggesting Adastra should not only lose its sibling status, but cast out of the {i}Galaxias{/i} as a whole.
That, along with having Parents who shared the same galaxy before arriving resulted in a closeness in our cultures that only emphasizes our differences.
And with all due respect to Amicus, I had always viewed the situation to be the fault of the imperial family for allowing an Omorfan to get so close in the first place.
"Anyway, when you came out of that lavatory, the look you gave me was strikingly similar, but I know that's not you, Scipio."
"You are a good, honest person, and I know you would never do such a thing if the intention is simply chaos and destruction."
"And despite our differences in culture and language, and despite the history between our people--"
"--you are my friend, and I trust you."
I almost smile, despite myself.
This is Neferu 'communicating'.
Perhaps he's an outlier amongst the supposedly blunt Khemians, but I'm able to understand what he's saying.
"{i}I know that you're here to gather intelligence, to better Adastra's position in the alliance, and to use me as a tool, just as Alexios used Cassius.{/i}"
"{i}I'm lonely, and I need someone that I can call a friend, a true friend, and in this relationship, I know that you have nothing to lose while I could lose everything{/i}"
"{i}But I also know that you are full of compassion, and you would never do what he did, and so while I know that you can't be trusted, I trust you.{/i}"
The real question is if he's making the right choice.
I look Neferu in the eye, in what I hope is a meaningful way so that he might know that I understand.
"And I trust you. I simply want the galaxy to achieve harmony, and... it sounds pup-like, but all I want is less hardship and anguish for sapients and all other living things."
My fur bristles in an uncomfortably prickly way, feeling sick just being in my own skin.
{i}I would watch the Clay District burn for the sheer pleasure of it. Why feel anything but joy in the destruction of uneducated, cruel, sapients who act like dumb beasts, lesser than livestock?{/i}
"Thank you, Skip, truly. I know that this experience will change your life, and your perspective on life itself."
"Adastra did that for me, both bad and good, but I wouldn't take it back, so just keep an open mind, and I'll always be available if you need help."
"Thank you, Neferu, truly. And please, if I offend again, just talk to me. We are friends, wolven friends, after all, and that means you can be very blunt."

"Sounds like a plan. Now, we should get some sleep so as not to throw off our schedules when we arrive in about six hours. Brunis is actually in my room, so I can sleep in his bed, if you don't mind."
I don't mind, and we both end up sleeping in my bed.
Mercifully, I'm left alone by the voices, that is until I hear Ahm.
"Exiting Stretch Drive in 10 minutes. Prepare for security check and royal escort."
After some quick grooming in the lavatory, I step onto the deck with Neferu and Brunis, looking out the windows.
No longer in the stretch drive, the nauseous bending of light is replaced by the massive planet below us, its atmosphere, full of dust, is clearly visible hovering far above the rock surface.
Still, I'm wary of any sudden movements, half-expecting an abrupt descent to the globe below, at least until Neferu tells me we're waiting for security clearance.
It's then that I'm able to have a good look at the planet below me.
I stare, not quite believing where I am, despite the tortuous lead up to this moment.
The idea of living on a planet has always been an alluring idea to me.
The planet our moon orbits, Ancoris, is uninhabitable.
The handful of banished wolves that live there need to wear special spacesuits to protect them from the elements and un-breathable air while they mine outside their bases.
Even then, when, or if they come back, their bones are left misshapen, muscles torn, organs damaged and cardiovascular systems ruined due to the much stronger gravitational pull of Ancoris.
I know I don't have to worry about that here despite Khemia being roughly twelve times the size of Adastra in terms of surface area.
One of the many aspects of Khemian culture that drew me in was the persistence of the jackals, to explore and, to an extent, to tame their planet.
For millennia, before the Khemians even thought of themselves as "Khemian", they built civilizations at the edges of the polar regions on their planet, living off the steady source of melted ice.
The lack of water and intense heat at the equator had kept the planet's middle mostly barren.

The axial tilt of Khemia was really the only reason intelligent life was able to develop at all, with the rest of the planet populated by mostly underground-dwelling insects and small, but plentiful, robust vegetation.
Most Khemian civilizations pre-{i}Galaxias{/i} were almost constantly at war over water between the aptly named "water kingdoms" of that period.
Now though, as I look down at the beige-colored desert planet, I see evidence of Khemian civilization all over the surface, even from this distance.
Lines and patterns unnatural in the universe cover its entirety, even its parched circumference.
What draws the eye the most is the current of what appears to be clouds, some sort of atmospheric disturbance allowing the tower to always face the sun as it orbits the star.
They did make use of their seemingly useless equator after all, its environment still too harsh to support comfortable living.
The jackals had been able to terraform their entire planet, and as a Luxian, I envied that, and it had me fantasizing about what Lux, what Adastra, could be.
I've seen it plenty of times in photographs, but to see it in person reminds me of how much I've wanted to visit this planet.
But there's a tinge of sadness in this moment, as I wish that this was all under different circumstances, the stress and exhaustion blunting the excitement.
That is until we orbit further around the planet and I see the giant contraption that siphons energy from their star before it's beamed down to the planet itself.
"Enjoying the view?"
Neferu approaches from behind and puts a paw on my shoulder.
I don't flinch or feel the need to draw back like I did in the past.
"That must be Sahira's Tower?"
"Yes. It provides all the energy to our planet. As you can see--"
As we rotate further around the planet, Neferu points to an odd orange, almost pink glowing beam.
"It's transferred from the star and carried to our planet via laser transmission."
I stare for a while, taking it in, but unable to stop the nagging feeling of unease.
How?
I notice Neferu looking right at me and I clear my throat.
"It's very, very impressive. I recall Omorfa experimenting with the idea, but declaring it too dangerous for the solar system's stability."
"Yes, though we were sharing the tech with them, at least until the talks with Adastra started."
I'm unsure what to say to that, so I remain quiet, staring at the beam until we orbit back around the planet.
"I forget how massive planets can be. I remember reading that exploring beyond the poles seemed as insurmountable as intergalactic space-travel for the Khemians at the time."
"This is true. One of the main hurdles during the unification of Khemia was its sheer size. I believe it took a century longer than Adastra to achieve."
"Yes, but weren't Khemia's methods largely peaceful, utilizing diplomacy over force?"
"Hey, that's right! No offense, but I'm surprised they taught you that."
I glance around the deck, noting that Amicus and Veteris have not yet joined us.
"They don't, but I supplemented my teachings with Khemian records and I was able to fill in gaps."
"Good on ya!"
Neferu makes a lowering gesture with a paw.
Brunis pauses, looking around the deck like I had before lowering his voice to a soft-spoken rumble.
"Again, I don't wanna seem like a condescending Khemian, but I know how Khemian viewpoints are basically quashed out of existence by your empire."
"I remember having to read {i}Adastra: A History{/i} back in school and--"
"I'm not trying to be a prick, but man, is it... well, it's super Adastran."
He's practically shout-whispering at me.
"You know, you make yourself sound like a bigger prick whenever you get euphemistic."
I'm listening, but my mind is preoccupied with this sudden interest, along with how Amicus or Veteris might react to me speaking poorly about Adastra.
I'm not afraid, knowing they'll be fine with it as long as it draws in Neferu, along with anyone else influential on Khemia, such as a high-ranking official like Brunis.
"It's illegal to read Khemia's counterpoint on {i}Adastra: A History{/i}, unless one is given access to the restricted library in Varro's University."
"Even then, those who read it are expected to treat the records, especially ones involving Adastran and Khemian interactions, as lies."
"I had to compile them all into an essay on why they were false, but I think it was worth it..."
"You read the Khemian counterpoint? By Hatherhotep?"
"I believe so? The one that matches its sections to {i}Adastra: A History{/i}."
I smooth a paw down my mane, fidgeting with it even though I know I'd made sure it was in place earlier.
"Are you, uh, fans of her writing?"
"You could say that. It's got some really important information in it."
"I imagine it's a very intense read for an Adastran."
"It's certainly shocking, but at least the counterpoint isn't blatantly biased, so I'm forced to consider that much of our own history omits and alters the narrative."
I feel filthy saying such things about my home moon, but I'm not fully lying either.
"I'm hoping I can receive lessons in the Khemian language in my free time while I'm there. All books and media with any Khemian in them were destroyed by the empire during the war."
"This is why none of the Khemian students or teachers born after the war can speak it."

"The big library in the city should have translators if you need info before you learn, but I'm starting to see why Neffy likes you so much. He's always trying to lay educated folks, or really whoever can outsmart him."
"What the hell, Brunis?"
"Can't ignore the patterns."
"Besides, you've tried it with me more than once!"
I glance at Neferu with a slight smirk.
"Really? I seriously doubt a graduate of Sabayet would like me for my Adastran-grade education."
"It's certainly not the main reason, but you are smart. And please forget any teasing comments I might have made about your school."
"Really Neferu? Shit like that only makes it more embarrassing to be a Sabayet alumni ."
"Sorry, it's a habit considering it's one of the few things I've done that my brother couldn't."
"I still find it kinda sad that your whole motivation for that was to stick it to your brother."
"Of course! And to see Ram's face when he learned I received my acceptance letter on the first try, after he tried several times over several years? Well... it was worth it."
"Are royal family members not granted a spot? I thought all of you were educated there."
"No, acceptance is based on merit alone. I mean, my father, mother, and my elder sister attended, and while being a royal makes it far easier to prepare, not everyone is capable."
"I see. Well, at least your brother has company if Aya didn't go."
"Oh, Aya has different ambitions. Ramoses, on the other hand, did not. He wanted to copy our father's path in preparation for becoming pharaoh."
"I mean, I was let in because of, uh... my past."
"There was a good reason for it. Besides, you proved yourself quickly after--"
"--getting higher marks than you."
"--getting the highest marks in your discipline. Also, our attendance was decades apart. It can't be compared."
"Definitely not. It was a little more rigorous back then."
I'm curious about Brunis's statements, both about his "past", but also about him being accepted into a school above his merit.
"Were you naturally academically-gifted, or was there another reason you did so well?"
Their reactions tell me I need to clarify the statement.
"Sorry, back when I was a pup, my grandfather paid for a spot in an elite preparatory school. I struggled at first, but later left at the top of my class. My motivation was simply to prove myself."

"Ohhh, got it, got it. Yeah, I really didn't fit in. Only way to shut those snobs up was to out-study and outsmart them. Honestly, Sabayet is the only place on Khemia where I didn't feel like I was Khemian."
I pause, the unexpected statement like a blow to the chest.
"I, uh, I can sympathize with that to an extent, I think."
"We gotta find some time to talk after we've settled down in the palace. You can tell me more about that school. I'm sure they brag about you being a former student now, eh?"
Another, much more painful blow stings beneath my sternum.
"And I can show you around the city for your research. Neferu would take you, but you know, he's gotta be more careful in public. Actually, aren't you famous now, Nef?"

"If you mean more recognizable, then apparently so. Photographs of me haven't been shown to the public since I was a teenager in family portraits. I imagine it's hard not to recognize me after what happened on Adastra."
The slide of a hydraulic-powered door announces Amicus's arrival.
"Scipio! A word please."
I stiffen up and immediately turn around and walk toward Amicus who beckons me into another area of the ship where he had been rooming with Veteris.
The very idea makes me want to chuckle, but Amicus doesn't seem to be bothered by Veteris's consistent waves of hypo-manic chatter.
"Yes, Your Majesty!"
When I reach him, I bow at the waist, slightly beyond the required seventy degrees.
Amicus waves away etiquette like this once he decides you aren't an adversary, or disrespectful person, but I'd been told to continue doing it while on Khemia, for obvious reasons.
"Ahm, privacy in this room, please."
"{i}I have been disabled by your emperor for privacy reasons until you leave this room, Scipio.{/i}"
"I haven't seen you the entire trip, but I trust all is going well?"
"Y--yes, sorry. I was working on... my mission."
"Ah yes, from what I just saw, it seems to be going fairly well."

Veteris makes a noise like he's going to say something and we both look at him, and I just hope he won't say whatever he's going to say next, because Veteris thinking about his own words must mean it's a fairly--
He shrugs.
"They shared a bed!"
I wince, not because of what he said, but because he practically screeched it.
I suppose the noises and machinery of the ship drown him out, considering I haven't heard him since we were both on the deck at the start of the journey.
"Really? That's... that's rather incredible, Scipio."
I'm still trying to figure out how Veteris knows that, but as long as they don't know about what lead up to it, I don't really care.
"Yes, nothing seriously intimate. We just wanted to be in each other's company."
"Even better. I knew that jackal to be a promiscuous man, but it appears he's also desperate for companionship."
I have no idea how to take that sentence, so I stand attentively, wondering why Amicus is judging Neferu for something wolves do all the time.
"Almost makes me feel sorry for him."
This time I grit my teeth, focusing hard on keeping my expression neutral.
{i}Letting my emotions get in the way already? ALREADY? Whose side am I even on?{/i}"
"Why feel sorry for someone who should know exactly what's happening here? Let him have his heart broken. I'm sure it's not the first time."
I think of the endless, flat tundra surrounding Lux, a landscape of boulders and brown, dead-looking vegetation.
A place where nothing is happening.
"Actually, I'm pretty sure that was the reason for his falling out with the royal family--"
"I see, I shall continue that part of my mission, then. How was the trip for you?"
"Hmm, it was mysterious..."
I suppress a sigh.
So little words for what might actually matter.
"We've found some strange inconsistencies, particularly involving Khemian tech. I'm sure you've met Ahm?"
I rub my left temple.
"Yes, I feel it's rather invasive. Is he not a spy if he's in our brains?"
"I have no idea, but I will be speaking to the vizier about having him permanently removed from our linguas. Absolutely outrageous."
"Think about the implications of that, though! How in the world did they manipulate the lingua?"
"Exactly. It's a metal orb that's less than a millimeter in size and is filled with an unknown liquid. No Sibling has figured out how it works."
"Apparently they can build everything the Parents gift us, but even better. Constructing a faster stretch drive is... it defies comprehension!"
"Yes, I've noticed this. It has made me feel uneasy."
"It's made me feel suspicious. If they're so advanced, why would they want an alliance with... the Siblings who have had the most hurdles to clear?"
Although Amicus won't say primitive, that's what we are; the most primitive Siblings in the {i}Galaxias{/i}.
Even the humans are more advanced than us, at least from what I've heard during the briefings.
So I think, trying to come up with an explanation.
"Don't they always emphasize galactic harmony? Neferu once told me that Khemians feel a duty to normalize relations between Adastra and the rest of the {i}Galaxias{/i}."
Veteris bursts out laughing, but Amicus at least explains.
"No, that's what they tell their people to justify what they're doing. There are hidden motives every step we take here, Scipio."
"Understood. Do you have an idea of what it might mean, Your Majesty?"
"I don't, but if the tech isn't made by their own design, then I can't imagine the answer is a good one."
"Something is treating them rather well, it seems."
Amicus and I go quiet, glancing at Veteris.
"Do you think the Parents can provide answers the next time you commune with them?"
"Hell no! I never get a straight answer from them. The only thing they're crystal clear about are orders."
"I see."
"So, I'm adding another task for all of us on this mission. Simply take note of any suspicious technology and record it. A small task, but it could be extremely important."
"Understood, Emperor Amicus."
I notice the ship becoming quieter suddenly, the absence of the whirring machinery and droning air vents almost stunning after becoming so used to it.
"I think we landed?"
"No announcement?"
"Maybe it's because we told Ahm not to be present?"
"Pff! Even wolves have figured out PA systems."
"Gods, I just hope it's not like this on all of Khemia. Putting their damn, state-funded, state-developed, and state-owned supercomputer into our damn brains!"
Amicus clears his throat after the outburst.
"Sorry. Now we simply act as if all is normal when we leave this room. Any other questions or concerns?"
"No."
"No, Your Majesty."
"Oh, yeah. No, Your Highness."
"I'll assume that sounded disrespectful because that's just the way your voice sounds. Now, you're both dismissed. We shall reconvene tonight."
"Remember, meetings are in the morning before breakfast and in the evenings after dinner."
The first thing I notice while stepping out of the ship is how dry the air is.
It actually reminds me a bit of Lux, minus the heat, a stark difference to the humidity in Adastra City.
Still, it feels good after being in the ship's overly-cool climate control.
We're in the palace courtyard, the walls of which block off most of the view, but the glimpses of the dunes I get seemingly roll on into the distance forever.
The capital city, Khemen, isn't visible now, with the palace blocking the view.
It's a fairly modest building, using angular and straight lines, but decorated in vivid paintings.
On the wall next to me, I see the hieroglyphs carved in sunken relief along the top and bottom, and in the middle, various scenes of jackals and many other species engaged in daily life, or rituals.
I have the urge to run my fingers along it, just to feel it, but I have enough common sense not to.
The monuments and statues are notably faded, stone worn down by time.
Much like Adastra, Khemia had ceased commissioning more extravagant and decorative projects to honor the royal family, though thousands of years earlier.
I know there are even more impressive structures in the city of Aarum, the most powerful kingdom in pre-{i}Galaxias{/i} Khemia.
"Skip?"
I jerk my head in the jackal's direction and I notice that my group has moved several meters away toward the entrance of the palace.
I hurry to Neferu's side.
"Sorry! It's just so... different from photographs, you know?"
"Oh, I do. I'll show you around the palace later if you'd like."
"Of course!"
I see the smile that Neferu is clearly trying to hide, probably amused at my pup-like wonder, but I can't help it.
The feelings that I had thought were missing are now back full force, at least for now, and I just take in the experience.
The buildings on Adastra, such as the university and imperial palace are old, but they had been rebuilt and modified over the past several centuries, but everything here is truly {i}old{/i}.
Maintained, but preserved.
"There's so much history here."
"Hm?"
"Oh, I see what you mean. Yes, much of the stone here has been in place for millennia."

"It reminds me of what my instructor in architecture once told me, that long-lasting, ancient structures take in the events and sapients around them, giving them more character than we ourselves have."
"Yes, Khemians very much subscribe to that philosophy. It's called {i}babekhen{/i}, literally the building's soul.
"Babekhen..."
I file it away, the word incredibly easy to pronounce by Khemian standards.
I notice that our envoy has stopped moving as I almost run into Amicus's back.
"Are they not going to welcome us? I was told the vizier would meet us at the entrance."
"Shit... Always making our jobs harder."
I glance at Brunis, but Neferu speaks up.
"Ram's making a statement, probably to show his reservations about the alliance, or he's just on a power trip. Typical, but do your best to ignore any of his disrespect."
"If the alliance breaks down, he wants it to be clear it was due to the outburst of a wolf."
"I see. Well, then we shall wait. I'm moving to the shade. I'm already sweating out of every pore."
"How do you think I feel? They'll assume I jumped into the fountain before they let us in."
"Should have gotten groomed before we came, Veteris!"
"Well, I don't... Actually, that might have been a good idea."
"But then I look too scrawny and malnourished. The facial fur is essential to my position as a scholar and instructor!"
I'm sweating heavily too, of course, and I wonder if this is part of what Ramoses wanted.
While Neferu's short fur makes the heat more bearable, Brunis has thicker fur like us, and I'm about to ask him how he handles it when Veteris asks something I hadn't even noticed.
"Say, what sort of technology is keeping that water fountain structure aloft?"
I had been so enamored with the building around us that I had barely glanced at the fountain, but now that I'm looking at it...
"I don't know. You would have to ask an expert in the field."
"And what field might that be?"
"Um, I'm not sure."
I see Neferu's confusion at Veteris's tone and question, and I want to tell my teacher to not make his suspicion so obvious, as Amicus had told us not to.
"Ahm, what field of tech is being used there?"
"I'm very sorry, but unfortunately that information is classified by the State for planetary security."
"Sorry, I suppose more advanced tech information is sensitive, which I'm sure you understand."
"Strange to display classified tech so blatantly, and for decorative purposes?"
I step in at that point, having hoped Amicus would do so, but he's pacing further away, clearly deep in his angry thoughts right now.
"Veteris, let's ask someone with better knowledge on the topic later, alright?"
I give Veteris a quick bow before turning to Neferu.
"Please excuse Veteris. His style of acquiring knowledge can seem a bit intense sometimes. We're just very excited to be here on Khemia."
"Hm, indeed. But I don't want to be interrupted when I'm able to question a qualified jackal, Scipio."
My face burns, and not at all from the heat, mortified that I have to correct my teacher only minutes after landing.
Better now than in front of the vizier or pharaoh, though.
"Teacher, remember not to use the word jackal. Khemians can be... how many species?"
"Fifteen, and they make up over sixty percent of the population."
Veteris isn't listening at this point, instead deeply inspecting a pillar, reading the hieroglyphs out loud in Khemian, and despite his fluency, his pronunciation is terrible.
Terrible to the point that my lingua can't translate it.
Brunis and Neferu glance at each other with slightly confused expressions, before Neferu again tries to stifle a smile, and I feel my ears grow hot.
I'm beginning to worry that I'll have to supervise Veteris the entire visit, though I try to play it off with a smile, speaking lowly to the two Khemians so Veteris won't hear.
"You can see why Adastrans need training from an expert. He learned from books only, before the war."
"It's no problem, just unexpected. But you are right. Maybe Adastra can set up some programs with native speakers if all goes well."
"Vizier Ramoses is now arriving to welcome the diplomatic mission from Adastra."
A second later, the stone door lowers slowly.
