It's dark in the entryway, and I wonder why there's no lighting at all.
Neferu sighs loudly next to me, muttering something about theatrics.
Then I see a glint of light reflecting off of something, something gold.
Then, Vizier Ramoses steps out into the courtyard.

I was nervous about this moment, despite having seen the vizier before at two meetings over the past two years, but with the unusual ceremonial garb, it's more intimidating, which I suppose is the point.
Shiny, smooth black drones float around him, moving close to us for a moment, as if looking for any signs of danger before moving back to the vizier.
We all stand awkwardly for a moment, and I look between Amicus and Ramoses, wondering who should make the first move.
I assume Amicus knows how to properly greet the vizier, but after making us wait, it's clear proper etiquette is not being used right now, and Amicus simply watches him carefully.
Then there's more movement behind him, and I see another jackal, a young female.
She walks up behind the vizier, and he bends his knees slightly so that she can reach his mask and pull it up over his head.
Then she moves to his left, where she stands and looks on politely.
She locks eyes with me and doesn't look away.
Her expression tells me she's found something, and I know this must be Aya.
Then Ramoses steps forward, head high, leaning back a bit more than he might need to.
I wonder if it has to do with his position.
"Welcome Emperor Amicus, and welcome Amicus's subjects. It is an honor to have you and your people on our planet once more. May Ahhotep be with you this day and with Adastra forever."
"And may Ahhotep be with you. Thank you for the invitation and for accommodating our envoy."
"It seems we may have arrived too early, so I apologize for that as well."
"No apology is necessary, you were right on time."
"I see, that is a relief then."
"However, it would not have been a problem if you had been early. The fact that you are here now, on peaceful terms, is all that matters to the pharaoh and his people."
"Of course, and may it stay that way forever."
The hot wind blowing across the desert is the only sound during the gaps in their conversation, seeming to emphasize how the pauses go on for just a second too long.
"Forever indeed."
"I must thank you for taking time away from your vital duties as emperor to talk with Khemia directly."
"All is well on Adastra, I trust? I hear your sister is acting in your place."
"Yes. Of course, I was reluctant to do so, but the importance of our discussions required it. I only hope that we can reach a solution during my time here."
"Of course."
"The pharaoh is still wrapping up his visit to Omorfa, but progress can still be made between the two of us in the meantime."
"Now, let us head inside and we can begin preliminary discussions, along with plans to visit the city for your public address in three days."
"Very well, and thank you again."
"No need for thanks; it's an honor to have you here."
Amicus begins following the vizier into the palace before Ramoses turns back to us.
"Neferu, please show the others around and make sure they're comfortable."
Then he disappears into the palace with Amicus following him.
I blink, slightly stunned by the brief, tense introduction.
Not much of an introduction considering he didn't even look at me, or Veteris, or even his brother until he gave him a command.
I had been ready for some kind of unpleasantness considering how Neferu talks about him, but if I were to judge him based on those few minutes, I don't think his demeanor is even suited for ruling.
If he's the next pharaoh, would he not just end the alliance as soon as his father steps down, or passes away?
"Bit of an asshole, isn't he?"
I whirl on my teacher, eyes wide, paws up, trying to shush him.
"It's fine, Scipio. 'Asshole' is a compliment for the likes of him, a prick all under the guise of politeness. The nicer he acts, the more he wishes you're dead."
"Ambassador Brunis!"
Brunis jumps, looking down at the much smaller wolf.
"Yeah?"
"I must ask some questions about Khemian political etiquette to better log this event in my records."
"Well, that wasn't exactly normal, but uh, okay. Do you wanna to go inside first or--"
"It shall be quick! I'm going to be taking notes out here anyway once we're done."
I watch Brunis awkwardly try to talk to Veteris, but the height differential is so much that he eventually sits on his rump to better talk to my neurotic teacher eye-to-eye.
"Neferu! It's so good to have you back!"
She jumps up and hugs him, which makes me relax, taking it as a signal that formal etiquette is no longer required.
"And it's good to see you again, too. I'm just glad to be back. "
"Yeah, I was so upset when you told Father you wanted to stay after what happened at that palace."
"We both know that would have only made everything worse. It's the only place I had a purpose, anyway."
"I understand."
"Now please introduce me to your friend!"
"Ah, yes. Rammy didn't even introduce any of us, did he?"
Aya gasps, then laughs.
"I forgot you call him that sometimes."
"Do be more careful around him, though. He's a bit testier than he used to be."
"Fantastic news."
"Anyway, this is Scipio, he's the student of the scholar over there, his name's Veteris. His directives are to--"
Neferu stops as he realizes that Aya has stepped forward, grabbing my paw.
I flinch in surprise, but I try to play it off with a smile.
Touching during an introduction goes against my wolven upbringing, but I grip back gently to acknowledge it.
At the same time, I wave at her with my free paw without even realizing it, as if I'm using every greeting I can to cover my bases.
"Hello, Aya. It's a pleasure to meet you, Neferu has told me a bit about you."
"It's a pleasure meeting you Scipio. I think we've already met, though not as formally."
"Oh, yes. So... that was you, in... in my dreams?"
The last words come out in a humiliating mumble then almost squeak at the very end.
Luckily, she only nods, and I'm relived I haven't exposed myself as insane yet.
I notice then that she's still holding my paw, as if she's feeling for something, and her attention doesn't seem to be on my face, as I would expect, but still, she seems to be focusing hard.
I look at Neferu, but he looks back with raised brow, seemingly as confused as I am.
She's frozen for a bit, then her grip twitches, and her demeanor changes completely.
She stares at our paws, then she looks up at me closely.
I duck my ears in embarrassment.
"I'm sorry. I'm probably out of touch when it comes to meeting someone in the Khemian--"
"Don't be sorry. This isn't a typical greeting."
Her voice, once high, melodic and eager, is now low and almost dull.
Still, she holds my paw and I make a small effort to pull back, to gently encourage her to end this strange, non-typical greeting, but she continues to hold on.
I stand there awkwardly, looking at Neferu for help.
"Aya, please, maybe you can do that sort of thing when you get to know him better?"
Aya doesn't acknowledge him, but she seems to come out of the trance, and with a sad look, she releases her grip.
She stares at me with the same sad, almost disbelieving look, and I fidget with my glasses to give my paws something to do.
"She doesn't normally do anything like that... That I've seen. Aya, are you alright?"
A part of me wonders if this is my fault, especially if this is the first time she'd done it.
"I'm sorry, I was just really excited to meet you."
She says this even though the excitement is gone from her voice.
"Oh, it's fine."
My voice is loud and full of false cheer, as if to make up for the lost enthusiasm.
"May I ask what that was about, though?"
"Of course, but it will have to wait until we have more privacy."
"We have privacy."
Neferu gestures at Brunis and Veteris, and I realize that my teacher's reedy, relentless voice is still chattering on while Brunis stares at him, mouth agape and squinting in confusion.
"From them, maybe."
She gives Neferu an almost guilty look.
"Hm?"
"Wait, me? But I'm his friend! You can't just grab people you don't know and drag them into your--"
Neferu cuts himself off, but Aya catches it.
"My what, Neferu? My witchcraft? My imagination? Do you also think I'm a schizophrenic our family is just trying to disguise?"
"N-No, of course not."
Neferu looks like he wants to say more, but he simply closes his mouth, looking stunned.
I'm stunned as well, and now I'd much rather be with Veteris, making sure he's not saying anything too foolish.
A strange, irrational thought that I could be the reason their relationship falls apart crosses my mind.
"I believe I started things off a bit awkwardly. Please forgive my wolven habits."
I bow slightly to her, trying to give the tension between them a release, and it seems to work, at least a little.
"No, Scipio, I'm the one with the unusual habits. I just have a lot on my mind right now, and there are some fairly popular rumors going around about my role in the palace.
She says that last bit to Neferu.
"They believe you're mentally ill?"
"It's the latest one, but it's a natural consequence to the secrecy of my role."
"I apologize for disrespecting it. I can at least sympathize with false rumors, though. We also need to talk."
"Of course, Neferu. You're staying in the palace while our guests are here, right?"
"Yes, as long as Ram leaves me alone and doesn't kick me out. I am technically part of the envoy, after all."
"Yes! It'll be just like old times."
"Well, maybe not {i}just{/i} like old times, but hopefully we can still enjoy ourselves."
"With Skip!"
I smile slightly at the casual nickname, wondering how every Khemian I've met uses it so quickly and naturally.
"I am here to understand and observe the ways of Khemia, inside and outside the palace, so I'm glad to be included."
"This is so exciting! Sorry if I'm sounding insane, but being in the palace with only Ramoses around, trying to make casual conversation with me..."
She shudders.
"It's a bit of a nightmare."
"That bad, huh?"
"It's probably because he has no one to talk to either, with father off-planet and Henut training in Amadun. Ramoses has always had someone to guide him, but that's definitely not going to be me."
I decide to become a bit bold, and break into the conversation.
"The time we waited for him when we first arrived; was it some sort of political tactic, or is he just..."
I search for the correct, least offensive word.
"Unaware of his actions?"
"No, if ever he seems rude, it's intentional on his part. Right Aya?"
"We literally stood at the entrance for five minutes."
"Oh."
"I'm sorry, but I don't know!"
"But you're a high-ranking ambassador and foreign relations expert!"
"Sure, but I don't know anything about some pharaoh from five thousand years ago--"
I turn to Veteris who is, unbelievably, clutching Brunis's pant leg to prevent him moving away.
"Oh gods, please excuse me. It was nice meeting you and I hope we can talk again soon, Aya."
"Of course!"
"I suppose I'll take the time to catch up with Aya. Good luck dealing with... that."
I look back, and at this point Brunis is trying to keep his pants up with a paw. I practically run to pull Veteris off of him, doing it in a way that doesn't drop Brunis's trousers.
"Magistrate Flavius. At this point, what I'm most curious about is why you're bothering to talk to me in the first place? I was under the impression that you were seeking a compromise."
Flavius, one of the triumvirs of Lupas, stares at her, looking somewhat bored.
Virginia assumes the only reason for this communication is to disrespect her.
Virginia stares at the man, noting the bald patches in his head fur, likely due to fur-pulling, made all the more noticeable in how he groomed the fur to try and disguise it.
He looks relaxed before her, but she doubts that's how he feels.

"A {i}realistic{/i} compromise. And I apologize for having to repeat myself, but I'll put it in a more concise format that you might remember: The last I checked a year ago, Lupas is our second wealthiest city, just behind Ad Rotae."
"Still, this particular demand is at least possible, but the others?"

"Why should Lupas have more voting power when your population is, last I checked, only about 1.5 million, half the 3 million average? I can think of four cities right now that actually do need more voting power due to their large populations."
"Finally, why does Lupas deserve veto power, a power reserved only for Adastra? What will the other cities think?"
"There is no explanation or excuse for it. I don't need to justify the reason. The answer is absolutely not."
The wolf growls in his throat, but it's so slight, Virginia is willing to let it go as something less, wanting to keep her conversation with this man as short and quick as possible.
Virginia struggles not to roll her eyes.
Lupas was a temporary capital for less than a decade over five millennia ago, while Tricelli served as a temporary capital for even longer, and far more recently.
But she's realized there's little point in arguing with this man, Virginia staring at his head fur instead, thinking about how to best deal with this situation.
Not just with Lupas, but the empire as a whole.
"You're right. At this point in time, we seemingly have nothing to negotiate."
"In the meantime, Adastra will be keeping a close eye on your city. Always remember that I will not hesitate to do what needs to be done to keep the empire stable."
"And if you refer to me again without using my proper title, you will be punished accordingly."
Flavius opens his mouth, his fur bristling, and Virginia feels some satisfaction in seeing it.
He likely has never had a woman speak to him in such a way.
"Anything else, Magistrate Flavius?"
He stares hard through the screen, and Virginia stares back.
"Very well. You are dismissed."
Just before the portal call ends and the screen goes black, Virginia hears a "Bit--" before the audio cuts off.
Virginia can practically hear the magistrate spitting out her most popular names: whore, prostitute, bitch, any gender-specific insult will do.
Not that she minds, but Virginia knows Amicus didn't do enough to keep this from happening.
Not intentionally, of course, and Virginia had refrained from pestering him about it, seeing how troubled he's become over the past several months.
She'd reminded him maybe twice, and he certainly thought he'd put together a reliable group of officials to aid her, but they hadn't been ready for this.
She wonders if anything could have prepared Adastra for this.
It's only been three days, or maybe only two?
She massages above her eyes with a thumb and middle finger.
No emperor, and certainly no acting empress, can succeed without a strong backing from... anyone.
"Incredible. All my life's work for this?"
She begins muttering to herself, something she didn't do before being left alone to "rule".
Of course, she never expected to be in this role. Potes's goal had been for her to at least become an advisor, which she did... And apparently failed terribly at because Amicus didn't think ahead.
"There should be ten advisors speaking to me right now. At this rate I'll be overthrown in a year, if not months. I wonder how I'll be killed?"
"I'm sure they'll be very creative about it."
"Apologies for interrupting, but Cassius is arriving in fifteen minutes."
"What? Why?"
She asks the question out of complete surprise, not expecting Com to know, and sure enough.

"I apologize, but I do not have that information. No forewarning of his return was given. He arrived on an Omorfan ship, which cannot be communicated with by Adastran equipment due to current strained relations."
Whatever the reason for Cassius's unexpected arrival, Virginia suspects it's not good.
Though, as she thinks about her brother, a few ideas form in her mind.
"Com, set out refreshments in the {i}Vestibulum{/i} to prepare for my brother's arrival, please."
"Of course, Empress Regent."
By the time Virginia arrives, she's a minute or so ahead of her brother, and he shows up just as the refreshments arrive.
He glances around before his eyes settle on Virginia.
"Sister! Apologies for my unannounced arrival. It's difficult to send message from--"
"Cass! It's wonderful to see you gain."
It's hard to say which of them is more surprised by Virginia's actions as she embraces Cassius.
Still, Cassius hugs back, though a bit stiffly, never having been one for showing verbal or physical affection toward his siblings.
"Are you alright? I don't think we've embraced since I woke up after the assassination attempt."
"Not exactly, but I can explain in a bit. Do you want to sit and talk over refreshments? If you're tired it can wait until morning, assuming you're planning on staying."
"Actually yes, I do miss those conversations we used to have. As for staying, that's also a yes."
"And thank you for accommodating me after... well, everything I suppose."
"You're a member of our family and you are always welcome here."
Virginia glances around, half-expecting to see Alexios somewhere slinking about in the shadows.
"Is Alex..."
"On Omorfa. You, uh, you won't need to worry about him coming back here."
"I see. Well, let’s have a seat and we can exchange our woes."
Cassius, clearly famished, is filling his mouth, so Virginia starts first.
"You might have heard that I'm currently acting on Amicus's behalf at the moment."
Cassius swallows hard.
"Mmh... Yes, I did. Congratulations... Maybe? I don't envy you, that's all I'll say. Also, I do not trust Amicus's judgement to gauge if Adastra is ready for an empress."
"Oh, certainly not. It kills these men to even acknowledge what I am."
"I see. Lux might be opposed, and Lupas definitely is, even if they haven't said so yet."
"You're right. I haven't had many issues with Lux yet, but I just finished a call with a Lupasian triumvir who called me a 'bitch' before our call fully ended."
"What? Which one was it? You're punishing him, right? That could even be considered a capital offense."
Seeing Cassius's hackles rise, she knows that prideful anger well, and it's coming to the surface, but for now it's somehow comforting.
"Sorry, I don't mean to upset you. Besides, it's simply one of my more popular nicknames, though not as popular as 'whore'. It's something I've grown used to."
Virginia sees Cassius wince at that word too, and it doesn't surprise her that he would have no idea, having had his full attention on becoming emperor himself before leaving for Omorfa.
"That's a bit of an odd one though, isn't it? Where do they think you have time to... do that?"
Virginia laughs, caught off-guard by the statement.
"Be a whore? That's a good question, but I assume they just enjoy the juxtaposition with my name."
"Amicus should have been actively punishing such behavior, but you're the acting empress right now. They must show you respect or suffer the consequences."
"I'm beginning to run out of other options, so it might have to happen soon."
"I'm surprised you haven't already. I still want to know which triumvir that was. Is he not aware that the traditional punishment for insulting a woman of the royal family is castration?"

"Emperor Pontus famously castrated a triumvir himself with a dulled dagger. And to be fair, the official made statements about Pontus's daughter's genitalia in regards to how many men she slept with."
"It always comes down to what's between our legs, doesn't it? Well, being an emperor rather than an empress is very different."
"It's fairly universal that men who rule with harsh, merciless tactics are seen as strong, and respected."
"Women, on the other hand, are seen as cruel and sadistic, which are qualities unbecoming of their natural role in the world... Which is nurturing and worshipping men, of course."

"And somehow history always remembers them as a seductress whore, or something. Those few female rulers on Adastra existed pre-Drusus, overseeing smaller kingdoms, but I assume it's the same now as it was then."
"Yes, I remember noting that back in my schooling days."
"Few emperors are treated fairly in the history books, but... yes, I don't believe a single woman was considered a good empress despite some of their kingdoms flourishing at the time."
Cassius talks of the subject as if it's the first time he's given it thought.
It seemed Amicus's egalitarian approach was the deciding factor on Cassius's position on gender roles.
"Either way, it would be my duty as your closest male relative to dole out the punishment, so you wouldn't have to worry about that."
Virginia doesn't even try to imagine such a thing.
"Once things have stabilized, however, and if all goes acceptably well, I will punish anyone who says such things. And it's a bit selfish in that my own honor is at stake here."
"What kind of brother allows such things to be said about his sister? A weak one."
While Virginia hopes this never comes to pass, she still rests a paw on Cassius's shoulder, acknowledging his love and support.
Cassius stares into the middle distance for a moment, his hackles lowering, before he looks back at Virginia.
"Are you... are you doing okay in your position?"
She notices Cassius isn't looking at her anymore, instead staring at the goblet next to him.
Even though it's {i}virdi{/i}, not wine, Virginia has a good idea of what he's thinking about.
He's never said so, but they all recognized that he had suffered mentally, not just physically, during the short period of his emperorship.
Seeing this, Virginia almost aborts her earlier plan, but remembering the possible consequences for herself, her family, and Adastra as a whole, she proceeds, but more cautiously.
"I'm managing."
"The main, insurmountable issue is that no one is on my side. They're either neutral or they oppose me."
"I would seek advisers, but Father's most consistent advice to me was to never allow males near me, either physically or emotionally."
"I especially want to heed that warning now, considering some families who ruled before unification might see this as an opportunity to take back power."
"However, he never planned on me becoming empress, nor did I, so I have no connections with anyone in power."
"Did Amicus not set you up with vetted members of the Senate? I know there's at least a dozen or so egalitarians in there."
"They stopped communicating with me one day after Amicus departed."
"Oh... That's not good."
"Indeed. I fear several plans are in the works."
"Stay in the palace as much as possible and always bring drones to escort you outside. Consider preparing your own food and knowing its source. I can go out and buy it if you need me to."
"Finally, you need an escape plan if the worst-case scenario unfolds. Have the emperor's ship always ready for departure. Then head to Khemia."
"Not just because Amicus is there, but also because they are the only ones in contact with Adastra, and I'm sure your plight would interest them."
"Of course, don't trust males, but also be wary of the possibility that they might use a female assassin for that very reason, so trust no one."
"The only men I've ever trusted are my brothers."
"That's very kind, but unfortunately your brothers are incompetent fools."
"I'm surprised that Amicus left, no matter what Khemia demanded, but risking the empire and throwing his sister into the mess to deal with it?"
"I--I just... This is what happens when he looks 'to the stars' instead of having a look at his own damn empire."
"It speaks of a deeper problem in his leadership. He'll need help with that when he gets back."
"He believed everything was in order when he left. The senators acted as if they were willing to work with me. I was prepared for the masks to drop, but not quite this fast and not all at once."
"I know my time is running out without some kind of political backing."
"I see."
Virginia sees the tension in Cassius's body, his breath a bit heavier now, and she feels a twinge in her chest at causing her brother such distress.
It's strange, having these emotions come back to the surface.
Apparently behavioral alteration didn't fully subdue "bothersome" emotions like it was supposed to.
But something about becoming empress, with so much responsibility, it's made her more aware of the emotions of those around her.

"I know this is a terrible situation to come home to, especially after your own experiences in my current position, but I'm truly worried for the future of the empire, especially if Amicus is gone for over a year."
"Do you still have connections in Adastran politics?"
"After how long it's been, I'll need to reconnect, but I believe I have enough influence to scrape something together fairly quickly. At least something to hold off any attempts to overthrow you."
"That would give us time to build a proper, sturdy foundation for your rule."
"So what would you have me do, Your Imperial Majesty?"
Virginia looks at her brother for just a moment, and while she feels love, there's a sentimental aspect to it, another emotion she thought had departed long ago.
But to see Cassius, who she knows to be a very emotional man, accept his anxieties and future misery in less than a minute to help her...
She quickly imagines cornering the emotion, locking it in an iron box, before letting it slip out of her head, the way she'd been taught.

Now is not the time, and she needs to get her emotions back under control, because she knows any word of her shedding a tear, especially in her first days as Empress Regent, would not do her, or Cassius any favors.
"You don't mind serving under a female?"
"You're my sister, Virginia, and now that I know how hostile the empire is toward you, I don't care about my reputation. My political career ended three years ago, anyway."
"My goal is to save the empire, and help you carry on the legacy of our family so that your one year of rule is remembered as a {i}great{/i} year."
Virginia has to smile at that, wondering if he still thought about the way she had initiated his removal from the throne three years ago.
But Cassius is very different now, just like herself.

"Well, hopefully with your talent for understanding the needs of the people, along with your political experience and connections, you can be my chief advisor, the magistros, if you're willing to accept."
Cassius gulps audibly.
"Alright then, I'll get started tomorrow. It'll give me a purpose, at the very least."
"Thank you, Cassius. I at least have hope now."
"Good. You worried me when I first arrived. I've never seen you in this sort of state before."
Virginia grimaces inwardly.
She definitely needs to get those emotions back under control.
"I think it's the isolation. Talking to Com and antagonistic officials all day does odd things to the mind. So tell me about Omorfa, if you're not too tired."
Cassius takes a deep breath, eyes looking up toward the ceiling, as if seeing something beyond.
"Ah, that reminds me I'll have to come up with some sort of explanation for what I did before I speak to any officials. As for my time there, it was... an experience."
There's a few seconds of silence.
"Hm, a good experience?"
"An eye-opening one."
Virginia lets another few seconds go by before asking the question she should have asked earlier.
"Did it involve Alex?"
"He is one of the main reasons. In the end, our loyalties lie with our own people."
"I came to realize how my irresponsibility and emotions ruined many lives on Adastra, but for some reason it took a few years."
"I had always believed that Omorfa forced him into a situation he did not want any part of, but now he tells me it was necessary."

"We were all naive to Alex's intentions. Omorfa hasn't attacked Adastra in millennia, and it was hard to believe they were running a sabotage mission with a cat who didn't have the physical or mental training to be a spy."
"But it was something he could only achieve by becoming close to me, which simply makes me ill to think about now."
That's not surprising as Virginia notices he's stopped eating, a paw subtly resting on his stomach.
She wants to ask Cassius how he's doing just like he had asked her, but she knows he'd be offended.
You simply don't ask males about feelings like this.

But while Virginia has never been in a romantic relationship, she does know the feeling of deep betrayal; the confusion, devastation, and hurt that goes along with questioning yourself and every single person around you.
It's how she always felt during her childhood and adolescence.
"I had told him how much it all bothered me, but he rarely thinks about it, and seems surprised that I still bring it up."
"It made me wonder if I had misinterpreted his fear and misery at that time, that maybe it was all for himself."
"And like most Omorfans, he believes the {i}Galaxias{/i} can only succeed if Adastra is no longer a Sibling race, no matter the means."
"I've heard that sentiment is growing stronger there."
"Yes, most likely due to the possible alliance with Khemia. Which, if successful, would be very difficult to undo."
"This is actually the main reason I came back. They don't even know I'm here... Well, they probably do by now."

"I, uh, actually stole Alexios's ship, capable of using the stretch drive. It was given to him as a gift for the destruction he caused. They weren't allowing me to leave because of what I learned being close to him."
Virginia sits up straighter, realizing she has another issue to worry about along with her rebelling empire, just as serious, if not more so.
"They held you captive? Are they planning something?"
"House arrest, basically, but yes, and while they were already interested after learning of Amicus's absence, I'm sure they'll be far more emboldened once they learn of the empire's true state."
"What better time to strike?"
Virginia takes a deep breath, looking down at the floor for a moment.
"Now I'm the one sorry for bringing such bad news home with me."
"I did say we should exchange our woes, and how woeful it is. Unfortunately, a male will definitely have to communicate with Planetary Defense."
"If you're willing, I have a simple plan for restoring your reputation."
Cassius's ears, muzzle, and tail twitch at the same time, but again, he forces a smile.
"I'm at your command."
After managing to pry Veteris from Brunis, my teacher and I have a solid ten-minute conversation on how one must behave on Khemia.
It's a delicate balance, and I worry that I will be fretting over what Veteris is doing my entire time here.
After reminding me that he's been waiting for this moment for over ten times my own lifespan, he agrees to tone down his excitement at least a bit.
I glance at the entrance where Brunis, Neferu, and Aya had disappeared into, saying they'd be at the entrance when we decided to enter.
"Shall we join the rest of our party, then?"
"Yes, yes, yes. I do want to warn you though, Scipio."
I turn to him.
"Of what, Teacher?"
Though I keep my voice light, I'm becoming a bit impatient, wanting to rejoin Neferu and Aya again, still curious about his younger sibling.
He lowers his voice, so I know he must know something he thinks is very important or interesting that he wants to say.
"I know we told you to..."
Veteris looks around.
"Ahm!"
"Yes, Veteris?"
His voice is projected from an unseen speaker.
"Oh good, you're not in my brain anymore. Give us some privacy until we enter the palace, please."
"Of course."
I glance in the direction of the voice, ears twitching before my field of view tilts wildly, Veteris reaching up to grab my arm to yank me down closer to his level.
"Ow! Teacher, please just ask me to lean closer, or s--"
"I don't trust anything here, Scipio. It's nothing like what I imagined it would be. Not in a good way. Something is very wrong."
It's very strange to have my teacher whispering hoarsely into my ear like this, but his urgency has me listening.
"I know we told you to get close to Neferu, but make sure you do not sacrifice your own emotions for the jackal, or any other Khemian. Again, something is wrong."
"We'll talk more tonight."
I straighten back up and nod, even though I'm unsure if it has to do with the suspiciously advanced tech or something else, I'm content to wait until later.
"Now, let's head into the palace!"
His reedy voice trembles slightly, betraying his suppressed excitement despite his sudden concern seconds earlier.
Veteris is a strange wolf, no question about that, but he's rarely shown concern or worry for me, and that alone is enough for me to heed his advice.
I look around at the empty courtyard for a moment longer, trying to see what Veteris might be so worried about, but I have to give up after a few seconds and follow him into the palace.
I'm first hit with the smell of something herbal with a hint of spice to it, an unfamiliar incense I can't place.
My focus is on the walkway that stretches out before me, seeming to reach an impossible length.
"The distance seems... excessive?"
Veteris waves his paw almost dismissively at the architecture.
"Remember Scipio, they use illusions to make their spaces seem larger than they are."
"Oh, yes."
Sure enough, I hear Brunis's voice, sounding much closer than I would have expected as we reach the end in under half a minute.
"Skip! We almost came out to look for you two. You know someone with fur as thick as a wolf is at risk of heat stroke out here."
"Oh, we were just enjoying the scenery and architecture. Even the entrance is curious."

"Yes, it must be strange compared to Adastran architecture. Those who built the palace and other historical buildings on this planet did so based on the visions seen by early contact with our Parent."
"The {i}Kemetarians{/i} are a mysterious bunch, aren't they?"
"Aren't all Parents?"
"To differing degrees, yes."
I quickly fill the silence as I feel Veteris almost trying to provoke the answer he wants out of Neferu, which isn't going to work.
"Well, I suppose with our Parent, the {i}Romanus{/i}, we know a little bit about them, such as their arrival to our galaxy in tandem with the {i}Galenians{/i}."
Brunis, deciding he safely wasn't of interest to Veteris anymore, finally relaxes and speaks up.
"Yeah, we know more about your Parent than our own, but that's probably because of what happened between Adastra and Omorfa, right?"
"Probably. You're speaking of the attempted interference by the Galenians and Romanus during our third war with Omorfa?"
"Oh yes, when they stopped our stretch drives from working and lit up our skies with omens of old wolven gods and pleas for peace."
"Maybe that's why we're so behind technologically; Parents with no self-control!"
I just let Veteris talk at this point.
While I know little about gathering information, maybe Veteris should have been learning himself.

"I believe they were well-intentioned, but desperate. The deep bond between Omorfa's and Adastra's Parents created intense, emotional distress to the point that they broke their promise to sapient agency."
"That war was especially horrific. If there was a time to step in to stop senseless killing, that would have been it."
"Most, including myself, believe the Kemetarians are the de facto leaders of the Parents, and likely brought the Romanus and Galenians to heel shortly after."
"I mean, didn't Khemia broker peace between Omorfa and Adastra like, right after that?"
"But likely with the guidance of your Parent, correct? You have a method of communication with them, I assume."
"Only pharaohs and the appropriate officials know the answers to those questions."
I step in again.
"The Kemetarians, don't they have a close relationship with the Taharkans' Parent, the {i}Kushari{/i}? They didn't come from the same Galaxy, did they?"
"No, but they originated from the same uplifter, and by chance, met in this galaxy hundreds of millennia later."
"Seemingly not as complex or as close a relationship as Omorfa's and Adastra's Parents, but yes, some sort of bond developed early before this galaxias's history."
"Which is why the lions came to your aid to win the second war between Adastra and Khemia! They are the second most advanced Sibling. That's rather curious, too."
"Well, yeah but that's because we, the Siblings, are also close allies."
Veteris's clumsy and scattered attempts to seemingly make the Khemians slip up is bewildering, and I'm having trouble following along myself.
This talk of history, along with Sibling-Parent relations that are complex and hard to understand reminds me that I don't need to understand.
I'm part of the plan, yes, but a small part that is currently spanning the cosmic microsecond that is my life.
{i}Promise to sapient agency...{/i}
I take advantage of the lull in conversation to change the subject.
"Neferu, do you know where or when I should meet Aya? She said she wanted to have a private conversation with me."
"No idea, and she never thinks to tell anyone. Her duties require her to be elsewhere several times throughout the day. She'll show up again soon, though."
I nod, and the conversation shifts to lighter things, such as when we can visit the city, and the news is surprising.
"Actually, I was briefed by Ahm when we got here, and I guess a few extremist groups have become more... extreme. Security will have to be tight so probably no casual visits to the city."
My heart sinks in pure disappointment, and it must show on my face.
"Sorry, Skip. Wish they'd told me while we were on Adastra. Feels like the whole planet changed while--"
"Which groups, Brunis?"
"Um, well, there's about two hundred thousand Omorfans on the planet, so that's gonna be a problem--"
"Wait, that many? You know they want Adastrans to be abandoned, if not completely eliminated, right?"
"There are a lot of Omorfan families who have lived here for generations, refugees from that second war, in fact."

"Still, before I left, a solid majority wanted a peaceful alliance with Adastra, but I guess there've been a bunch of protests over the past few months. I'll have to look into how the hell that happened."
I've forgotten about my desire to see the city now.
Now it seems like our mission might not even be possible.
It sounds like Khemia would have to risk its own security for the alliance, and what civilization would do that?
"What of Khemian groups or organizations?"
"Maybe we should talk about this--"
"Ahm, what extremist groups are posing a threat to our Adastran visitors?"

"There are a few, Neferu, but as Brunis mentioned, the main concern is the Omorfans currently residing on Khemia. {i}The Children of Sahira{/i}, are also a threat after an incident early yesterday that is currently under investigation and classified."
"We'll talk about it later, alright, Nef?"
"No need."
"What's wrong? Do you know about that group?"
"I will tell you when we are in a better location. It's something I find hard to talk about."
I look around and realize Veteris isn't around us anymore, hence why Neferu said that out loud.
I feel a slight pang of nervousness not knowing where he is, but I remind myself he's the senior scholar here.
Maybe the Khemians appreciate his forwardness, especially after seeing Ramoses's behavior.
"We could go somewhere now, if you want?"
"Not right now. I can hear Amicus and Ramoses coming back."
Sure enough, I hear them too as I perk my ears.
I quickly stand at attention as Amicus appears first.
I can tell by his expression that he doesn't mean to stay, simply nodding at me and Veteris.
"I'm going to check to see if messages have arrived from Adastra yet. We'll meet tonight at..."
"Twenty-two hours are in a day, Amicus. Food will be offered at the seventeenth hour."
"Thank you, Ahm. We'll meet after dinner at the eighteenth hour."
Amicus then walks briskly down the hall, toward our sleeping quarters.
My ears lower as I hear Ahm directing him through the halls, which are followed by his low growls of annoyance.
There's a strange quiet in the air, and I turn and almost jump as I see Ramoses staring right at me.
His muzzle is pointing lower now, and I think I understand why he makes a point of keeping his chin up.
His sunken cheeks and thick nose make his muzzle noticeably bulbous and heavy-looking.
I quickly lower my gaze, waiting to see if he addresses me.
"I apologize, but who are you exactly?"
I feel my face heat up underneath my fur.
Even though he wouldn't know who I am, he asks the question in a way that sounds more like "{i}why are you even here?{/i}"
"I am Scipio, scholar of Khemian history and culture. I am a student of Veteris."
"Brilliant student! Adastra's future must be present for such important things."
Veteris's sudden reappearance is as mysterious as his disappearance before he's gone again.
Either way, Ramoses seems to lose interest with that last part.
"Interesting. Neferu! I need to converse with you in the throne room."
"Oh, right away your holy--"
"Shut up!"
I jump and quickly look away, wishing I'd followed Veteris to wherever the hell he went.
Even Brunis looks surprised.
"I know you had a great deal of fun tormenting me when we were younger--"
"But I am the vizier and you will treat me with respect, or you will leave. Your choice."
Neferu looks at his brother with an expression I can't quite describe, but it's deep and angry, and it's something I've never seen from Neferu before.
"Very well."
And with that, Brunis and I are left to stare after the pair.
"Guess things have changed."
Virginia sits at the garden on one of the benches under the shade of the trees, wanting a break from the almost oppressive stuffiness of the throne room.
She knows she's supposed to be going through building and budget proposals from several minor cities, but she only finds herself staring at the page.
She can't stop thinking about the series of events that lead to this.
While she's confident that Cassius's support will be enough to at least allow Adastra to function, she finds herself more concerned with what the other Siblings are doing.
It all seems so... odd.
Everything is lining up too perfectly, and not in their favor.
Could this be the end of Adastra?
"Good afternoon, Sister. I have some good news--"
"--and maybe some bad news, but Lupus has agreed to cooperate if I become co-ruler with you."
A visceral shudder starts in the wolf's shoulders, but he squeezes his arms tighter together to hide it.
"Oh, Cass. I'm sorry you must go through this again, but you're doing work that I simply cannot do--"
"More like they don't allow you to do your work."
"Are you alright? You look... unwell, the stresses of ruling a rebelling moon aside."
Virginia looks up at Cassius, at how he stands stiffly, arms crossed tightly, and can think back to all the times she'd seen him just like that growing up.
This is difficult for him to do.
Not just politics and governance, but asking if she's alright.
While her personality had been intentionally altered to feel less emotion, Cassius had experienced a childhood that made him hide from emotions.
After their mother passed away, their father was always cold, even annoyed at the mere presence of Cassius.
He's grown into a deeply emotional man who pretends emotions don't affect him.
How could he not turn out that way?
"Not exactly, Cassius. I'm distracted by the behaviors of Omorfa and Hindi."
"Can you tell me more about what happened on Omorfa, anything you overheard?"
"Well, once news came that Amicus was leaving for Khemia, there was a notable excitement in the air. Alex still being tied to politics allowed me some insight."
"I distinctly remember hearing one of them say 'as long as the others fill their role, we can be done with all this."
"I don't know who they were referring to specifically, but it sounded coordinated, hence why I escaped."
Virginia reads a line on one of the documents and realizes she's read it at least ten times now.
"What do you make of it?"
Virginia leans back, rubbing her brow vigorously, now realizing why that cretin triumvirate was pulling out his fur.
"First, I apologize for not being fully present when I should be driving the push to stabilize Adastra, but I can't help but think about external threats."
"I have no doubt that co-ruling with you would bring instant order, but..."
Virginia sits forward, looking Cassius in the eye.
"When was the last time the pharaoh made a public appearance? Or when has anyone seen him?"
"I'm not fully sure on that, but last I heard about him was maybe two years ago."
"Did you hear he was visiting Omorfa? He was supposed to be there at the same time you were."
"No, I didn't even hear mention of him, and I should have, considering where I was."
"And he hasn't made any public appearance on Khemia for a year due to traveling the galaxy, for one reason or another. This is all based on the vizier's statements."
"You think this has all been a setup?"
"Possibly, but if it is, I don't think that was the initial goal. Now, with the vizier in power and the pharaoh missing, who's not to say this is a plot to destroy Adastra?"
"This was coordinated by the Parents though, wasn't it? They couldn't possibly let it spiral to that extent, no matter how incompetent I think they are."
"Perhaps they've given up? Either way, they say they will not interfere, but tend to do so anyway. All I know is that they can't be relied on to make this work."
Cassius is quiet, thinking.
"While it's hard to imagine Khemia being involved in treachery such as this, if they believe it's the only path to a stable Galaxias—like the Omorfans do—I suppose it's possible."
"I'm seeing strange patterns in Lupas's finances. Wealth that came from a source with nowhere near that much money, or no source at all."
"I believe they want a repeat of what happened three years ago, only far worse."
"Well, we do have an escape plan in place, though I'm not sure where we'd go if Khemia isn't safe either. A Child settlement might be our only option."
"I am not running and hiding for the rest of my life that way. In fact, I would rather die here on Adastra."
"Well, I won't see you die here, otherwise I will as well. But for now, we should do our best to keep Adastra stable, and if it happens, we'll have a plan by then."
"I truly hope I'm wrong. It does seem impossible that the Parents would allow this to happen, but... maybe they are in disarray as well?"
"Maybe the Romanus have been ousted, and maybe our moon will become as uninhabitable as the planet we orbit."
"Virginia, please. Let's just focus on Adastra right now. You have enough to think about."
"If it happens, then it happens. Our moon is well-fortified, and we've withstood attacks from almost all siblings trying to invade our moon."
Virginia holds back from telling Cassius that was likely only due to the fact that to defeat the wolves, total invasion and destruction would be required.
Whether out of moral principle or possibly even exhaustion, each Sibling left with nothing signed, Adastra in ruins.
"Only Adastra can truly destroy itself, and I fear the consequences that will befall our people."
"While I don't believe a full-scale invasion is possible, I doubt the Siblings would even attempt one, knowing what will happen, just like three years ago."
"Do you have people in Lupas who can investigate further?"
"A few. I can at least ask them about Omorfans that might be living there. Lupas accepting help from Omorfa seems more far-fetched than anything else we've discussed."
Virginia shrugs.
"Lupas's triumvirate system is corrupted to the point it's now run by only a few families, the wealthiest ones, of course."
"And of course, Amicus couldn't just purge it because that practically guarantees bombs in the center of Adastra City until we relent."
Cassius becomes quiet, staring into the distance before speaking.
"It's a strange life we lead, Virginia. How did we get here?"
"Chance, consequence, and of course that bastard Potes who put us here."
"At least one of our questions has an answer, eh? Now, we'll keep our ears to the ground, but in the meantime, I'll help you with signing off these documents."
Dinner is interesting.
First of all, we're alone, Neferu and Ramoses somehow still carrying on their meeting.
I hope Neferu is okay.
Those thoughts are quickly stolen by the food itself as I take my first bite.
Veteris takes his at the same time, and then starts howling about the spiciness of it.
Sure enough, my eyes water and my nose runs, and it only seems to get worse. The food, a poultry dish of some sort, is so spicy it numbs my tongue, while still managing to stay painful.
"Why in the world would anyone want to suffer agony while they eat?"
I can't help but agree with Veteris.
While I enjoy some spice in my food, I don't enjoy being in pain, writhing in my seat as if trying to escape it.
Despite Amicus's calm, straight face, his eyes and nose tell me he's experiencing the same thing.
"I s-suppose there's an appeal to the rush of endorphins th--."
I fall into a coughing fit.
"As appealing as the rush I get when I stub a claw!"
"Well, at least the Khemians aren't here to enjoy our pain."
"Apologies, directions were followed according to Vizier Ramoses's specifications. {i}Dakhet en-Shemau{/i} can be prepared with a mild amount of spice."
"Apply that to all dishes that are spicy."
"Yes, same please."
"Me as well."
"Noted, all future dishes for all wolves shall be mildly spicy."

After we eat the food surrounding the molten meat, which was admittedly delicious, Amicus and I wait for Veteris to finish while he still picks around the sides, despite them being meant for, I assume, cooling the mouth.
Finally, Amicus stands and so do Veteris and I.
"Ahm, please tell Ramoses the dinner was wonderful. And please avoid telling him about our struggle with the spice, we don't want to be rude."
Veteris elbows me in the thigh, which is the height his elbow is at.
"More like we don't want to give him the satisfaction, eh? He was probably looking forward to seeing us choke that down if Neferu hadn't pissed him off for whatever reason."
I just nod, then follow Amicus out into the halls of the palace.
"Apparently there's a room just for discreet meetings, with background noise to ward off eavesdropping."
Amicus looks at a door, then startles slightly as it opens soundlessly and I can already hear sounds coming from within.
Pools and fountains, decorative, and lavish, causing a cacophony of pleasant water sounds.
Amicus leads us to the center where benches sit and towels lie.
I use one to wipe off a bench while the others do the same.
Then Amicus focuses on us.
"This was a mistake."
My eyes widen, and Veteris is silent for once.
"Our meeting consisted of Ramoses listing off grievances we never discussed before and that he says needs to be addressed."
"Have any of you gotten a straight answer on what the pharaoh is doing, or where the hell he is?"
"Omorfa! Is what Ramsos or whatever said."
"Ramoses, Teacher."
I say it as respectfully as possible, bowing to him at the same time, actually worried he might get himself into big trouble around someone like Ramoses.
"So he says, but there's no return date, or actual information out there that he's on Omorfa. That would be a headline on any galactic news channel."
"I would say maybe it's confidential, but if that were the case, Vizier Ramoses shouldn't have told us."
"Like I told you, Scipio, something is wrong here."
"Best case scenario is that he's telling the truth and we simply have to put up with that pompous jackal. I don't know who the hell trained him, but they sure fucked up!"
I'm ashamed as I start to question my own emperor's ability to handle this situation.
He can keep his emotions in check when needed, but when those walls drop, it seems all he feels is frustration, irritation, and anger.
He wasn't always like this, according to Neferu.
"Worst-case scenario? We're falling into a trap, but I trust the Parents and Khemians enough to hope that is impossible."
"Stranger things have happened."
"Yes, and with Ramoses in control, it would be the only time such a move would make sense."
"Maybe we should have an escape ready, at the very least?"
"They tightly control all vehicles that have a stretch drive equipped."
"I... I believe that if such a thing were to happen, Neferu would help us obtain one, if he can."
"Oh yes, ask him, please. That would be at least one worry off my mind. The rest being the collapse of the plan."
"Or Adastra as a whole!"
Amicus shakes his head, like he doesn't want to believe anything.
"If they even try... it will be the end of Galaxias as far as I'm concerned."
I don't know what that means, or what Amicus is thinking about, but my assurance that Neferu will help us seems to calm them, and it makes me feel useful.
Amicus asks if we have anything more, and Veteris lists off a few things he found that seemed suspiciously advanced, such as the floating globe in the courtyard.
I mention the extremist groups that Amicus seems surprised to hear about, maybe even a little mocking.
"Weren't we always told there was no extremism on Khemia?"
When the meeting is over, the mood is gloomy and dark.
Despite knowing how unlikely it is, our mission has clearly shifted into something we never prepared for, and we can only hope it rights itself somehow.
Or that we're simply wrong.
I sit alone in the courtyard, holding a uniquely shaped stone, one covered with eroded holes and spiky protrusions around it, but my mind is mostly blank.
After the initial landing and introductions, followed by seeing Ramoses, then the meeting, my hopes for the mission have fallen significantly.
I especially remember Ramoses's eyes burning into mine, asking me who I was.

It seems to me that we should have waited until the pharaoh arrived, whenever that might be, because the vizier is so abrasive and strange that I don't think it's possible to negotiate anything fair with him.
And what's the point of me manipulating and prying into Neferu's life when he's so clearly out of favor amongst those who truly rule?
Well, I like him, and we need a ship.
"Hold still for a second."
Neferu's smooth, gentle voice makes my chest feel as if I've slipped on ice.
The feeling happens again as I glance back and I'm surprised to see that Neferu has no loincloth on.
Rather, he's holding it in his right paw.
"Close your eyes so I don't get sand in them."
I do as I'm told and I hear and feel him sweep it on the ground next to me.
I open my eyes and see a small creature, like a large beetle skittering away, and then I see the tail.
"A scorpion!"

I say it with a pup-like wonder that's a bit embarrassing, especially when Neferu laughs, but scorpions had become one of the symbols of Khemia that drew me to this planet before I'd even started proper schooling.
"Sorry, I've just never heard someone excited over those creatures. Nothing wrong with being interested in them, but do keep an eye out when you're outside in the sands, especially at night."
"I completely forgot, thank you."
Neferu puts his loincloth back on, and I can't help but watch the ritualistic movements as he wraps it between his legs, over his thighs, then fastens the ornate clasp at the front.
"So... why are you sitting out here alone and looking so gloomy?"
I lean back on my paws, gripping through the sand that's still warm from the blazing heat of the day.
"It's nice to be outside when it isn't too hot, especially for a wolf. Also, everyone is doing something else right now, so I'm just soaking in the Khemian air."
Neferu inhales deeply.
"I have missed the desert air, I have to admit."
We sit in silence for several minutes, and it feels good, but I'm too curious and worried not to ask.
"That was a long meeting with your brother."
"Ugh! Yeah, he wanted every detail. I didn't tell him half of what happened though since he's not my father."
"When is your father going to be here, though? I don't think I've heard of what exactly he's doing in over a year..."
"Not to say it's my business, but your brother saying he's on Omorfa is the only thing I've been told."

"Should be in the coming days, according to Ram. I'm not sure what my father is doing, but it's clearly something classified considering I've heard no news, nor have I seen him mentioned when visiting the other worlds."
I shift, trying to keep my tail from twitching, instead staring at the sky.
"Heh, it's almost like you're waiting for your own father to land."
I frown at the idea.
"Definitely not my father, I'd be waiting for a crash-landing in that case."
"Oh, I'm sorry. I've never delved into your family life since you seemed a bit guarded about it."
"He was cruel to me and especially my mother before leaving and never coming back. But it was a good thing. It was peaceful with just me and my mother."
"Ah, maybe my family is right about me being too self-centered. I don't even realize that others around me have similar struggles."
"It's okay, I was very young so I had no real attachment to him... Neferu, if things became dangerous here, or if we become trapped, or even attacked here--"
"What? Did something happen?"
"No, I'm worried because your brother is a bit..."
"Shitty?"
"He doesn't demonstrate control over his emotions, and he seems to think being rude is part of ruling. I'm worried if your father doesn't show up, this mission will be a failure."
"And his hostility honestly has me worried, and I'm hoping there is a way out of here in case something happens."
Neferu seems to think, seems to figure out everything we Adastrans are worried about.
"The last time I saw my father must have been three years ago, and the times I did see him were very brief, usually to give me some sort of task. This is nothing unusual for him to do."
"But yes, he has a far better temperament than my brother. Still, Ram is solidly behind the alliance, that I at least know to be true."
"You do?"
"Yes. He's worked his entire life to this point. Why would he throw it away and risk derailing the entire Galaxias, which is what would happen."
"But just in case, would you help us, even... even if your brother would not want it."
"Of course, Scipio. I would have to come with you, since a scenario like that would definitely end in my banishment, but I think we'd have bigger issues to worry about in that case."
That relieves me, and I reach out, hugging him around the shoulders, Khemian-style.
"Thank you, Neferu. That makes me feel a lot better."
He hugs back twice as hard.
"But really, try not to worry. Ramo is a unique personality, simultaneously ambitious, but stupid."
I snort unintentionally.
"Gods, Neferu, that's cold."
"That's simply how the truth feels, Skip. Anyway, I would be more worried about possible Omorfan saboteurs than anything else."
That reminds me of something.
"So what are these groups that might cause us harm? I thought Khemia was mostly free of radicalism?"
Neferu's mood dampens visibly.
"There are extremists everywhere, of course, but they've never been this bold."
"Much like some of your cities, like Lupas, fringe groups flourish on parts of this planet that must be gently handled, and perhaps it was too gentle."
"Lux has the same issue."
But then I have the same issue, in the opposite direction, willing to watch the uneducated men of Lux stuffed into their disgusting taverns and set ablaze, just like they did to the schools.

"To be fair, Lux was practically set up for such conditions. But times are changing in the Galaxias, and I... I need to tell you about one of those groups, but honestly I need a bit more time to explain myself."
"You were part of one?"
"In my youth, but it's caused me tremendous grief and I regret it deeply."
The heaviness in Neferu's voice makes me wonder how far he went, if he hurt people.
A clicking sound mixed with scraping is heard as I grip the rock too tightly and chip the claw on my middle finger.
I hardly notice.
I'm honestly shocked to think someone like Neferu would join a group like that, but I know my reaction is important, and like he said; times are changing, and that's because people do too.
"No problem. Maybe you can tell me after you've had a little time to think on it?"
"Yeah."
"So why is he so, um, abrasive?"
Neferu easily adjusts to the change of subject.
"Because that's who he is. Especially with father not around, he's feeling more bold and more stressed out from the position he's in."
I ponder that.
"I suppose that makes sense. I'm surprised he snubbed us upon our landing though. Isn't that reserved for those you don't like, to tell them their time is not important to you?"
"I think he just enjoys having any sort of power, especially considering how weak he was as a pup."
"Oh... Why did your father choose him as the successor, then?"
Power hungry, irritable, and even cruel while holding onto past grudges; this has all the makings of a mad emperor, or pharaoh, in this case.
"Actually, I'm pretty sure he's preparing my oldest sister for it."
That gets my attention.
"Really? He should, because I think anyone in your family is better suited to becoming pharaoh than he is."
"They'd have to chain me to the throne. But now that Ram is messing things up so badly, Henut can finally--"
"Neferu!"
I turn and see Aya, and my mood lifts, seeing someone who had been kind to me aside from Neferu and Brunis.
"You can't just share sensitive family secrets that I tell you. You're going to get me in trouble!"
"Relax, Aya. We can trust Skip."
"Luckily."
She turns to me.
"Anyway, did you want to learn a bit more about what's going on, Scipio?"
"Oh, yes, of course!"
I get up, brushing the sand from my robes.
"I assume I'm not allowed to come?"
"Of course not."
"Well, I suppose I will just have to wait alone. If you're still up for talking and it's not too late, you can come by my sleeping quarters if you like."
"I knew it. Neferu, why didn't you just tell me he's your boyfriend? I could tell right away."
I shift uncomfortably as Neferu glances at me.
"Oh, sorry. I'm such a Khemian. Whatever you guys are, it's good for you, Neferu."
"Ahem, thanks, Aya."
He turns to me.
"I still do want to answer your question, when you have time."
"Of course, Neferu."
Now he turns to Aya.
"And don't take this the wrong way, Aya, but don't do anything that might be strange or weird, alright?"
"Nothing strange or weird. Scipio already knows most of this stuff."
"Alright! I'll talk to you later Skip."
I follow Aya through the palace, the halls quiet to a degree that's almost suffocating.
I try to fill the silence by commenting on it.
"It's very quiet in this palace, in general, I mean."

"You have my father to thank for that. He had a very difficult time paying attention when there were distracting sounds. He had most of the palace's surfaces covered in a layer of nanomaterial that absorbs and cancels the sound."
"I see."
I wonder if we even have the resources to create such nanotech.
We finally come to a stop at an inconspicuous door, though there are hieroglyphs, ancient ones, surrounding the door that hint at something more beyond.
Aya stops suddenly, as if remembering something, and turns to me.
She takes a moment to look me over.
"Okay, do you have any idea what this might be about, Scipio?"
"Not confidently, but I think it must have to do with your ability to speak with me in my head over long distances."
"It does, yes, but much, much more than that. Scipio, you have specific abilities that have gone undetected until now."
"This is usually the case, but Khemia has recently achieved the ability to measure and detect it."
I wonder if these abilities are simply talents, like maybe my good grasp of history.
"I'm not sure you have the right wolf, Aya, I don't think I--"
"Have you ever met someone who did the same as I, or experienced the same as you?"
"...No. Was it unusual that I was able to hear you?"
"Very. But the most important question I have is if you want to learn more, or leave it at that. While it's not dangerous, it seems you're having negative experiences related to this ability."
"Do you mean like {i}ahewawi{/i}?"
"Oh, no, not that specifically."
I see Aya moving away from the door, taking steps toward me, and I think she's second-guessing herself.
"Is it bad for you? I can help you find resources for treatment, or let Neferu know so he can--"
I let out a fake laugh, one that I think sounds genuine, though it's hard to tell with how the walls suck up the sound of it.
"Oh no, that's just what came to mind. I have a mild case of it that causes negative moments in my life, so I thought that might be it."
"I see. I haven't prodded further into your past out of respect, but I can sense some unresolved pain."
"I just want to warn that sometimes the experience can be intense and outside forces may take advantage of this."
There's a pause, and I blink at Aya, waiting to learn more about these outside forces.

"I know this all sounds very confusing, but there are a few rules that must be followed so what happens beyond this door cannot be discussed with anyone except me. I just want to forewarn you and give you a chance to back out."
This is all becoming much more serious than I had initially expected.
Still, the mysterious nature of it all, and the almost frustrating ambiguity makes me feel as if I can't back out now.
"I understand. I would like to know more, and I'll make sure to keep it confidential."
"Alright, we'll do the official oaths once we're settled."
Aya steps toward the door again and Ahm speaks up.
"Aya, Scipio is unauthorized to have access to this room."
"Please grant him access for a single entry, please."
"Very well."
Aya looks over her shoulder at me.
"I'll make it permanent depending on how well this goes. Don't worry though, just normal precautions."
I nod, simultaneously checking my body language, stilling my tail, keeping my ears up, and my shoulders loose.
"And don't worry about the sound you hear as you pass through the door. It's all part of the process."
I lower my ears, about to ask Aya what exactly that noise was doing when I see the room.
It's almost like I've entered a dream and the walls of this room seem to fade out into the distance.
Lines and curves are hazy and undefined, and there's a sort of pressure in the air.

"So, what you're feeling right now is the {i}veil thinner{/i}. If you remember, the stretch drive makes it easier to communicate in this way. That sound, the feeling you have, makes this process much easier."
"I see."
I don't have anything to add because I never have anything to add to these things.
It's fascinating, unnerving, and uncomfortable all at the same time.
"I'll start with the basics. We'll take an oath. It will sound serious, but really it keeps a sense of trust and openness in the realm we enter while preparing the mind for calm, sacred work."
"By the royal blood of my family line, and the ocean of the Amalgamation, the words spoken in this room are sealed."
"Now go ahead and repeat something along those lines."
I feel a bit of panic as I try to think of an appropriate and earnest-sounding oath of my own.
"By the sacred tasks of my imperial duties, and until the silence that follows my last breath, all that is spoken within this room is sealed."
I'm relieved that Aya seems pleased with this.
"Alright, so here we go. I am the current {i}sakhaet{/i} of Khemia, the 83rd in a long line post-Ahhotep's Unification."
Sakhaet sounds familiar, and based on my limited knowledge of the Khemian language, something involving transmission or communication along with a hint of divinity or vast spaces.
"My main purpose, which began in my fifteenth year, is to communicate with the Parents."
I'm quiet at first, in case she has more to say, and also to think about that.
When she doesn't say more, I realize she's giving me an opportunity to ask questions.
"I see. From my understanding, the Parents are not just on a different plane of existence, but are also difficult to communicate with, even directly, but that's impossible as far as I know."
"That's true, however, I don't communicate with them through words, but rather through feelings and guidance."
"You do this without tech or any other form of assistance?"
"Yes."
"I see. What of the Monitors? Can they not do the same thing?"
"They can, and they're far better at it, but their methods are fully controlled and authorized by the Parents. This method allows for more direct and quick communication."
"And they talk to you willingly?"

"So that's where it gets really interesting. While they don't talk to me, or even acknowledge me, I can {i}feel{/i} their motives or emotions to an extent. There is still communication to some extent, but it's hard to describe."
"It can be difficult to piece together, but it has been a great asset to Khemian civilization as a whole."
"Is, erm... Is that why you're so technologically advanced?"
"Hm, I've never personally been able to glean insights into technology, though it's possible past sakhaets have been able to, especially if they were tech-savvy."
Probably not, then.
I then do some quick math in my head, considering the unification happened five thousand years earlier than Adastra.
"Is it a lifetime position, if it's held for over 150 years on average?"
"Generally, though there have been gaps, and some choose to leave once another is found."
"Do you wish to leave?"
My questions are a bit bold, and I remind myself that she is still in a position far above mine, even if her demeanor causes me to forget that she's not a child.
"Not yet, though I've only been doing this for five years, so I suppose my mind might change in a hundred."
"Understood. So you sensed that I might be the same? Do you know everyone who has these abilities then, just by sensing them?"
"No, but I believe that your closeness to my brother, and my fate in general, are what tied me to you, in a way."
"How well known is this? Do other Siblings have their own sakhaets?"
"Yes, the Hindo have an ancient tradition surrounding it, while the Omorfans still use hallucinogens from plant life to reach a similar state."
"The Taharkans call theirs the {i}dakhur{/i}, and they understand it in a very similar way to Khemians. I sometimes talk to the current dakhur, in fact."
"You do talk to others, then?"
"Only ones with the same gift and after I've formed a bond with them. He's a friend of mine. He's interested in meeting you at some point."
"Oh."
I've never met a lion before, and doing so in this state is intimidating.
"But don't worry. We'll do all that next time."
"Sounds good. So, to be clear, Neferu doesn't know what you do, right? He seemed surprised that you were communicating with me at all."
"Was he upset? It would be just like him."
"Couldn't you sense it?"
"Remember, I can only read people with similar gifts who I know personally, you being the exception."
She explains it to me patiently.
"That's right, sorry. So how much of this can I say to anyone? And specifically, someone like Neferu?"
I don't bring up Amicus of course, and not only because I know the answer is no.
This may be something I never tell anyone about.
"Neferu knows I communicate with the Parents, but that is all. You'll sort of be able to tell what you can and can't share."

"As for your emperor and Adastra as a whole, the same applies. I only ask you to participate in three sessions, this being one of them, before you consider telling them. This is only so you have a broader understanding of its significance and impact."
"Though we are about to take an oath, if you ever feel your safety or health are at risk, do not hesitate to ask for help or reveal information you feel might be crucial to help others."
"Be warned though, that if you choose to be fully open to your envoy, you will be dropped from training."
I hope she tells me how she'd know, but she doesn't.
I shift from foot to foot, trying to make it look like I'm just loosening up.
"I don't think the wolves have ever had such a position, or recognition of such abilities. Older religions might have, but it was achieved the same way as the cats."
Aya nods.
"Wolves aren't the only Siblings who don't recognize the value of sapients with more... flexible minds."
"I see."
"And I must admit, it would be much more tolerable if I had someone to talk to and discuss these topics with other than just the dakhur."
"With an alliance forming, this would be a good bond to share for all three of us."
"And that's why you're somewhat unique, and why I have so much interest in you. I sensed and found you before I met you. It feels intentional."
"Is there intention behind this? Like do the Parents somehow control it? Sorry, I'm just trying to make some sense of this."
"While I don't believe the Parents control it, I do think it has to do with how they exist. The mind is sort of able to move through different planes, similar to what the Parents do."
"Is there a lot to learn?"
"A little bit, but that's the great part. I got the hang of it within a few sessions, which is the norm, from what I've been told."
It must be a natural talent she believes I have then, which I both hope to disprove, and prove at the same time.
"I see. Okay, so how do you do it?"
I'm almost eager now.
"Now that's where people differ the most. You have to find your {i}key{/i}. This will unlock and lock the {i}gate{/i} you will open. I think you already know yours, Scipio."
"Meditation?"
"Precisely! So, you already have your key. You have unlocked and locked the gate before, so you already have some experience."
"Interesting..."
I remember the comment she made to Neferu about rumors of her being schizophrenic, and part of me wonders if this is all one big delusion.
I doubt that it is, but my mind struggles trying to process this conversation that would be laughed at by the others.
"What is your key, if you don't mind me asking?"
"Mine is palm-reading. Dakhur Zanmek's is through holding certain stones and crystals that he feels energy from."
You do eventually learn to access the gate without the ritual you once used, though Zanmek still holds crystals during communication for his grounding technique."
"Still, we practice our keys from time to time to keep us spiritually awake and practiced."
A sudden realization hits me, and I reflexively clench and open my paw.
"Is that what you were doing when we first met?"
"Heh, yeah, you caught me. I know it was strange, but I didn't plan to hang on that long."
"It was just a surprise when I felt your energy for the first time. I was having a hard time deciphering what it was telling me."
I want to ask if that's a good or bad thing, but I notice Aya staring at my paws, and I stand straighter while clearing my throat.
"Did you want to read it again?"
I offer a paw.
"Actually, yeah. Thanks Scipio. It will put me in the right head space, and then we can start on your key."
"Remember, though; I'm not telling you your future, but rather the feeling I get about the current path you're on, and people change paths multiple times in life."
"It's the key to the gate that matters most."
Aya gently holds my paw, again feeling it more than looking at it.
"I'd use powder to better see the creases in your pads, but since I don't have my palmistry kit with me, I'm just going to go off mounts."
"Mounts?"
"The feel and shape of your pads."
"Oh, got it."
But she's already at work, and I feel her press into my thumb pad, and then she becomes quiet, eyes closed.
When she speaks, it's with less passion, in an almost monotone voice.
"Hot, but rough and flat. Emotionally guarded, but love is working its way in. I assume it's Neferu. He's the same."
"Do you mind if I feel your primary mount? It helps me see the path and possible fate you're heading toward."
"Go ahead."
I say it automatically, regretting it, but knowing I need to be open with Aya right now, and considering I don't know what my path or fate is...
She shifts her paws and this time she focuses on my middle finger with more interest.
She pauses for much longer this time, and I get the urge to pull back again, despite her reassurances that none of this is set in stone.
Still, if it's connected to the Parents, or anything that's fact, then why wouldn't she be able to see the truth?
"Cold, and fleshy, lots of depth. More repression than I've ever felt before."
I begin my own grounding techniques, made all the more difficult by the quicksand-like material beneath my feet.
Maybe I should bring my own physical objects to better stay connected to reality like Zanmek does.
Her eyes then rest on my claw, gently feeling the rough, uneven break where the tip had been scraped off.
I almost self-consciously tell her what happened, that I haven't had a chance to clip it yet, but I keep quiet for now, not wanting to break her obvious trance.
Aya fully opens her eyes, and the look she's giving my paw isn't a good one.
Then she suddenly whispers in low and rapid-fire Khemian.
"{i}Keru em senet-kha, mesekhet an-ru, sa'ah Ahhotep."
The Khemian words are completely untranslated by my lingua, and I'm left staring at the jackal.
It must have been a phrase or ritualistic saying if it wasn't intended to be translated.
But, slowly, her eyes focus a bit and she smiles at me.
"What did you see?"
Aya seems to think hard about her words.
"I don't know yet, but I'll try to uncover as much as I can in future sessions. Sorry if I worried you. It happens from time to time."
Her expression and those whispered Khemian words, which I'm now convinced were a blessing based on the few Khemian words I know, make me think it usually doesn't happen.
"Alright, now, do what you always do when meditating, but try to reach further, if that makes sense."
I remember how it felt in the ship, and I nod, crossing my legs, and beginning my breathing exercises.
Aya gets comfortable on the strange, sandy floor as well, which is almost powdery, like flour, yet I see no evidence of it sticking to our fur or clothing.

The last I see of Aya, she's in a similar position across from me, but with her eyes closed, her own paws pressed together, looking completely absent, and I get the feeling that I'm being left behind.
How embarrassing would it be to go through all this build up only to find out I can't do it?
"Relax, I'm here. And that's the whole reason why I'm here. To help guide you."
I glance at her, wondering if I even saw her lips move, then focus back on my breathing.
Just like in the stretch, the barriers around my mind feel thinner than usual.
After steadying and analyzing my breathing, I focus on the barrier, feeling its shape, its purpose, its simple state of being--
I slip through the gate faster than I intended or wanted, but I'm there now.
"See? It's simple for someone like you."
I choke back panic as I lose track of my body.
"It's okay. Remember breathing?"
Sure enough, I feel my chest still move, I still inhale and exhale steadily.
"Sorry, that caught me off-guard. Where are the Parents? Where are you?"
"So that's another level that we'll discuss next time. As of now, you're free to move and feel about the universe."
"Don't worry about going too far. Your brain is still connected to your body, and you can always snap out of it. This won't become a risk until we reach different planes in future sessions."
"Okay... but the whole universe is here? Can I explore it?"
"Feel free. And if you need help, just think of me and call for it."
"Understood."
I'm moving, and I sense Neferu, sitting in his room, waiting up for me.
He's hunched over, looking upset, and though I prod him, there's a solid barrier that's impenetrable.
I'll need to talk to him after this, but for now, I move on.
Distantly, I hear a rumbling voice, the deepness offset by the excited tone.
"Aya, can I meet him?"
"Next time, Zan. He's exploring..."
I'm already far from the place I started, and somehow, I know where to go.
I'm in Lux, and I find her small cottage on the outskirts immediately.
My mother is sitting at the kitchen table, kneading dough, making the bread rolls I love so much.
I can almost smell the {i}oliban{/i} in the air.
But her eyes are red, and the way she sniffs tells me she'd been crying.
