It hurts my chest physically, and I want to reach out to her, but there's a barrier around her, too.
I'll ask Amicus if I can send a message to Adastra earlier than the schedule permits.
"{i}It may not even be about you, Scipio. Maybe she carries {i}ahewawi{/i} too?"
The voice of dead leaves returns, and I mentally flinch back, thinking about calling out to Aya.
"{i}You're safe, Scipio. Just hear us out before you make a decision. Why do you trust her? Why would she give such important, untapped knowledge to the wolves?{/i}"
"{i}You expect she'll train you then just let you leave, back to Adastra?{/i}"
"I do."
"{i}The Khemians along with everyone in the galaxy hates Adastra, which means they hate you. Open your eyes.{/i}"
"What..."
"{i}Literally. Open them.{/i}"
I stare.
Then I blink a few times, before staring again.
It's impossible, what I'm seeing, and what she's doing.
"{i}It's unnatural.{/i}"
What is she...?
It's as if she's making a mockery of meditation, but she's actually levitating.
"I see you, Scipio. I {i}see{/i} you."
So much emphasis is put on that word, and I flinch back again.
"What?"
I quickly close my eyes again, knowing this isn't real, somehow.
She speaks again, and when I peer through cracked lids, I see her mouth doesn't move.
"I see your motives, your struggles. I know what you're doing."
Her tone is cold, angry, and accusatory, and the smile fixed on her face makes it hurt all the more.
"{i}Pain{/i} can't {i}be{/i} undone."
I close my eyes again, afraid.
I'm in a dangerous spot, I know that.
I'm no longer in that room, and that's not Aya.
Something has gone wrong, and I'm stuck.
What do I do, what was it that she told me?
{i}Think of release, think of all the pain leaving you, dissolving, reorganizing itself into something neutral, as all things should be.{/i}
"{i}Look deeply, and try to understand the meaning. Fear and pain are a natural part of death, but after...{/i}"
I cast around for something else, something that might tell me what this means...
"Aaaaargh!"
Blinding pain, from the inside out like I've never known, and I feel my insides, my lungs, my heart lurch and spasm violently against it.
"{i}That's it, Scipio, then it's over.{/i}"
"Aya! Aya! Help! Help! I need help! I'm stuck!"
I'm alone, and I always have been.
"Scipio!"
A loud voice right in my ear.
I'm suddenly in the fetal position, face against the ground, and I realize I'm covered in sweat and tears.
I keep my face pointed toward the ground, waiting to catch my breath, vigorously wiping away the tears.
The only thing worse than crying as a male is crying in front of a female.
It doesn't matter that she's Khemian and would tell me it's okay to cry as man.
That's not my world, and the confusion combines with the humiliation, and I even feel a little anger toward Aya.
She must have known to some extent what's happening to me.
Did she mean for this to happen?
But then my hackles lower as I realize she couldn't have.
At least I don't think so.
Finally, I look up, and see Aya knelt next to me, her own eyes filled with moisture.
"I'm fine."
I say it quickly and with a surprisingly sturdy voice.
"Just... just lost my breath--"
"Scipio, remember we can only do this with trust and honesty. I know that's an impossible ask when you've only known me for a day, but I am an expert at this, I need to know."
I feel another burst of irritation.
"You're nineteen, Aya--"
I was going to say more, that there must be things she doesn't know, but the look on her face instantly crushes my chest that already aches.
"I suppose you're right. I apologize for causing you this distr--"
I can't, can't, can't, lose the one person who might have some answers for me.

"Aya, wait, I'm sorry. I... things are happening to me that I don't understand, and every time I feel like I'm about to get an answer, something like this happens, something that leaves me with even more questions."
She lets me gasp in silence for a minute or so, but the look on her face of dejection is burned into my brain.
"I'm sorry, I just need a bit of time to put together what happened. I know I need to tell someone about it, but I'm scared I'll be seen as mentally weak."
The experience is leaving me painfully open, honest, and vulnerable in ways I'd never dare to be on Adastra.
"That's at least a feeling I think I know, Scipio; my mental faculties being seen as a detriment and unfit for what I was born into."
"It's different, but you can always tell me whatever is on your mind, or if something's wrong without fear of judgement, either with Neferu, or if you'd like, me."
Why do Khemians always want to be so emotionally close and open?
It leaves me mentally torn, wanting to spill everything, but I need to remember Adastra, where I come from.
Still, I need Aya to do any of this.
"I think only you can understand what this might be."
"Possibly. Again, I'm sorry. Distressing things can happen in these states, and while I know you're... struggling with different influences, you can tell me, and I can help you."
I look at her, with an expression I'm not sure I've made before, because I've never felt the combination of emotions inside me right now.
Defeat, misery, and maybe a little hope?
I don't know, but whatever it is makes her eyes glisten again, so I quickly look away, beginning to pick myself up.
I straighten out my robe, sighing out loud in relief as I find it firmly over my rear.
While the men might not care, I had worried it had ridden up in front of Aya.
"Can we meet again, maybe tomorrow? I have too many questions."
"Of course, Scipio!"
"And if you need more time, that's okay too."
"Same time tomorrow?"
"If you're sure, Scipio. I'll check in to see how you're doing."
"Thanks, Aya. I'm sorry I lost control of my emotions for a moment."
My face is still red, and I'm still coming to terms with the fact that this happened in front of Aya.
"No, Scipio, don't be. I... I have a lot to tell you as well, about my own fears that you might actually find useful."
"Maybe tomorrow, if you're ready, we can talk about these things."
"I don't really want to say it, but I am lonely, and I need to talk to someone like me."

The reversal of her needing {i}me{/i} catches me off-guard, and while that nasty part of me that came to the surface wants to believe she's only playing to my male, wolven pride, I swallow it back down.

"Can I not accompany him as his emperor?"
"And I his teacher!"
"I'm sorry, but he specifically requested a private meeting. He says no more than ten to fifteen minutes."
"Outside, though?"
"Don't worry, Scipio. He might be strange, but as long as you don't take any of his baiting, it should be fine."
"And say as little as possible. He likes to take any spare word and twist it."
"We'll be waiting right inside the palace, and you can report on what he says when you get back."
"A-Alright..."
I make my way to the door, scared and angry that I'm being made to feel worthless and toyed with at the same time.
It's like I can't trust anyone.
I look around the courtyard, hoping that for whatever reason, Neferu is out here too.
I haven't seen him all day, and I assume he's been with his brother.
"Hello?"
My voice sounds small, lonely, desolate.
"Just outside the gates, Scipio."
I stare into the night, truly wondering if I'm about to die, or be taken prisoner for whatever reason.
I can't imagine I'm worth much, but this is far too strange.
Slowly, I follow the path into the open desert.
I stand there, waiting, eyes darting in every direction.
A shift of gravel and sand, followed by movement to my right.
I bow, deciding not to speak first.
His eyes are piercing, and they look me up and down.
Then he seems to relax a bit, though I stay tense.
"Beautiful evening, isn't it?"
"Very much so."
I keep my eyes lowered, doing everything I can not to offend him.
All I know is that I've somehow found myself caught in one of his games that I've heard so much about.
I just have no idea why.
"Are you ready to see the city tomorrow? It will be nice to get out of the palace, hm?"
"I am, yes, though the palace itself is very beautiful and I have no qualms with staying longer. Thank you for accommodating me, Vizier."
Ramoses snorts in a way that would be considered rude, but I don't react.
"Why do you think I've chosen to speak with you out here, young wolf?"
I wonder if he even knows my name, but I already know the answer to that.
"I'm not sure, Vizier. Do you wish to tell me?"
"Do I? Hmm, it's hard to say since I can be so {i}difficult{/i}, correct?"
I keep my face expressionless, and I revert to silence again.
"I like to keep things private, wolf, and so do all of you, it seems."
While initially the situation felt strange, now I know that it's outright hostile, but still, I don't know why.
We've all said offensive things about Ramoses in places that had now clearly been bugged.
"You think me to be a fool, wolf?"
Again, I'm silent.
I can barely hear him over my breathing and pounding heart.
I no longer suspect him to be a mad ruler.
He is mad.
"What are you and Aya doing?"
So that's it.
If I'd been smarter, I'd have realized that would have been the most interesting thing about me to him.
"Aya? We have become quick friends. She has taught me quite a bit about palm-reading."
Ramoses stares at me for a long, long time.
I'm almost certain the contact room cannot have recording devices in it.
If there are, then Ramoses put them there, and that means we have far more to worry about than what he thinks I'm doing.
What I can't figure out is why he's revealing this to me.
I stand there like a sculpture, a statue cast in bronze, my emotions nonexistent, just like I'd trained them to be.
"You wolves. Did they only bring you along because you're too thick to realize you're being made fun of, or because you're one of the weak ones, too frail to fight back?"
I subconsciously size the jackal up and have the distinct feeling that without his security drones, I'd be able to break his snout sideways.
But I stand there, getting some pleasure out of seeing him work himself up over my lack of reaction.
"You know, I could have you imprisoned for espionage. Aya and her work are sacred and secret, and it would be a disaster if it fell into the paws of your barbaric empire."
He can't do that, and if he did, it would be a grave mistake.
I have diplomatic immunity, and everyone knows it.
Being imprisoned for something a member of the royal family willingly shared with me would have no grounds, and even if Khemia has changed, I know it would not be a popular decision.
His father would reverse it the second he arrived anyway.
What strikes me most about that sentence, however, is the way he referred to Aya.
It sends a chill down my spine in a way nothing he's said about me has.
"Someone is spying on me, wolf, before you even got here. Who else could do such a thing, from such long distances?"
He's mad. He's mad and I'm here alone with him.
"And you are able to see through the eyes of the Parents? A wolf? That is--"
He laughs, not helping the image of a pharaoh who has lost his mind.
I wonder if he's revealed this side of himself to anyone else.
I hope so, otherwise I doubt they'll believe me.
"Go back to your lover, wolf. Keep playing your games with Aya. But be warned; the second you become a threat to me, Aya, or Khemia, I won't hesitate."
"And tell them whatever you want. My point has been made."
I bow, turn, and leave.
Amicus is furious even though I don't mention half of what the Vizier said.
Veteris is stunned, one of the few times I've ever seen him in such a state.
We agree to keep what happened quiet, but Amicus makes it clear that I am not to follow the Vizier's orders any longer.
He also makes it clear that if the actual pharaoh doesn't show up in three days, we're leaving, the alliance be damned.
As for me, I'm not too upset, I'm just further deflated knowing that I'm the one he decided to take his unhinged paranoia and rage out on.
I finally make my way to Neferu's room, and it's hard to describe how happy it makes me to see him there.
Not just Neferu, but Aya, too.
"Skip! Finally we see each other. It seems our duties are keeping us busy."
"You alright?"
I suppose the stress of the night is showing on my face, but I do my best to smile and nod.
Aya narrows her eyes, however.
"Did Ramoses corner you?"
My facade drops, and it comes out in a huge, exhausted sigh.
"Why does everyone here seem to know everything that's happening to me?"
Well, at least Neferu doesn't, judging by his reaction.
"What? What happened?"
"He thinks Scipio is spying on him, somehow. I don't know why. I told him you aren't, and I was being honest. He said he wouldn't--"
"Do you think he'd go so far as to bug this room?"
"No, that would be illegal. Even the pharaoh can't spy on private rooms. And what do you mean cornered? What happened, Skip?"
"Honestly? I don't know. I don't know why he decided to unload his shit on me when he's barely held a single fucking conversation with me. I'm just fucking tired, that's it!"
I pinch the bridge of my snout, leaning back against the wall.
"I'm sorry, I'm just... I'm just tired."
"I'm sorry too, Skip. We can talk later. I'll let you get some rest."
I'm disappointed, not just because she's leaving, but because I'm losing control of my emotions when I'm with my friends.
"Thanks, Aya. Know that he's bugged the contact room as well."
"I see..."
She sounds distant, her disbelief clear.
"Are you going to the speech tomorrow?"
"I am, yes."
"I'd like to talk to you then, you know?"
I make a point of looking at the ceiling.
"Just something... concerning I noticed that involves you. It might be nothing."
She gives me a look that makes me wonder if she already knows what I'm talking about.
Judging by what she's said about Ramoses, she probably does.
"Alright Skip. I'll talk to you then. Get some good rest tonight."
"Thanks. You too"
Neferu and I stand in the dimly lit room while I lean my head back against the wall again, eyes closed, feeling a dull throb behind my eyelids.
"Why don't you come to the bed?"
I nod, then follow him to sit on the edge of his bed, resting my head in my paws.
He waits another moment before speaking.
"Did you want to tell me what happened, or..."
When I speak, it's low, almost inaudible so that Neferu has to lean in to hear.
"I would. It's just... I don't want to get anyone in trouble. I'll explain when we've left the palace at some point."
I hate Ramoses, but also myself for being afraid.
"I hate him."
Neferu echoes my thoughts.
"When father gets back he'll be lucky to--"
Neferu glances around the room, shaking his head.
"Again, the most confusing part is that he's focused on me. I don't understand what I did. And why would he tell me?"
"I don't know, but I'm going to find out."
"Don't worry, I won't provoke him, but after what he told you, he's already broken several laws, and it's now obvious he's trying to sabotage the mission, so at least there's that."
"Targeting you makes absolutely no sense."
"What's the relationship between him and Aya?"
"Nonexistent, at least up until I left for Adastra."
I nod, staring at the wall.
"Why do you ask? Is it about what you're going to talk to Aya about on our outing?"
"Yeah, I'll let you know then too. Something about him... makes me want to crawl out of my skin."
I say the last words low, under my breath.
"Hmm."
"You spent the day with him. Does he seem the same as he was?"
"Sometimes. He's clearly drunk with power, but it's the same Ramoses I remember. I certainly wouldn't have expected that from him."
How the hell is it that I, a random wolf from Adastra, sees this side of him for the first time when he's been rambling on with Neferu, Aya, Amicus, and Veteris for days, years for his siblings?
I'm so unsettled that I search around for anything to talk about, and I realize that Neferu never did tell me about his past like he said he would.
"Are you feeling particularly tired right now?"
"Not necessarily. Why?"
I realize he's misinterpreted my intentions, and I feel a bit bad as I clarify.
"If you're able to talk about what happened in your youth, I'd like to know."
"Oh."
"Only if you'd like. I've just talked about myself so much today."
"And I suppose I haven't talked much at all doing Ramoses's bidding. Be warned, it's not exactly a happy story."
"I'm used to that."
"Just don't take any of this the wrong way. It was over a decade now, but it will help explain why I'm here in the first place."
"Okay."
I brace myself as Neferu moves to a sofa opposite me, allowing me to see him as he tells me his history.
So, where to begin? Back when I was around sixteen or seventeen, I was unreasonably rebellious."
"More so than now?"
"Much. That was around the time that I started dabbling in anti-Adastran literature, and by the time I was eighteen, I was a high-ranking member of the Children of Sahira."
"Is that the same Sahira who the tower is named after?"

"Yes. She was probably the most effective anti-Galaxias separatist in Khemia's history. Despite her politics being unsuccessful in the end, she did manage to create a Khemia that did not need the Parents to sustain or even advance its tech."
"That's not exactly important in this context though. In the end, we were just separatists that used terrorist methods."
I nod.
"On... on your own people, I assume?"
Neferu visibly winces at that.
"Yes, though I did not see them that way at the time. There was peace between the Siblings."
"I thought that whoever wanted wolven inclusion to either be mentally unwell, or deep down wanted the destruction of the Galaxias as a whole."
Neferu goes quiet then, staring into the ceiling.
He must be lost in that time, over a decade ago.
I think about my own feelings, of believing that certain people as a whole deserved to be punished.
"Did you, um..."
I abort the sentence halfway through, deciding it's too cruel to ask, but Neferu knows exactly what I'm thinking."
"Hurt people? Not directly."
He lets that one sit for a minute, and this time I wait patiently, the gravity of what he's telling me not lost on me.

Basically everyone on Adastra knew Neferu was being punished for something, that he had poor relations with his family, but few would guess that the first Khemian to set foot on Adastra in over 100 years was at one time a separatist.
"Because of my position, I was able to... to steal money to fund the group. While I might not have hurt people directly, I have no doubt that money hurt and killed dozens."
I can see the physical toll it takes on him to tell me this, looking away, so tense I can see his muscle standing out more than normal through his fur.
It's no wonder: He's confessing to being complicit in multiple murders.
While a part of me judges him at first, I again have to take a look at myself, and what I'd do to the cruel men that live around Lux.
I don't have the excuse of being an adolescent, however.
He finally chances a glance at me, and when he sees my attentive face without any trace of disgust or judgement, he lets out a soft laugh in a sad, defeated way.
"I was punished severely, of course. Father even sealed me in the palace dungeon for months. I thought that I was going to die, to be honest."
"I spent nearly a year imprisoned, then Father came to me with a proposal; learn everything there is to know about Adastra."

"For the next five years, I studied intensively, then after I'd learned the language and history, I was tasked with being the first Khemian to visit Adastra since the war, along with taking the first steps toward an alliance."
"And that's why you have me here now."
"Many thought it was only meant to be some type of punishment for you."
"It was. But that doesn't mean it wasn't sincere. By then, I had changed my view completely on an alliance, because I saw the alternative was only more suffering."
"So there you have it. Not very exciting, but also not very forgivable, is it?"
I think for a moment.
"How many know of this?"
"The first part? My family, Brunis, and that's it. My father kept it under the radar, somehow, even when the separatist ring was arrested."
"It was Aya who eventually convinced him of an alternative to the dungeons."
I smile at him.
"I'm sorry all of that happened, for everyone hurt by it. But I'm glad you told me, Neferu, and I am glad you're here."

"I hope you can keep it within these walls? I know it's not fair that I didn't fully face the consequences of my crimes, that hasn't been rectified, but I'm trying through this alliance the best I can.
"I'm sorry."
"You don't need to apologize to {i}me{/i} Neferu, but I think I understand you. I have my own feelings about certain groups I wish weren't so intense."
"I know, Scipio. But we change, and I hope that you can as well."
"Agreed."
I say it truthfully, even though the hate lingers in my muzzle like blood.
Once Neferu is asleep, I meditate.
I'm not sure how Aya and I will continue our sessions, and I want more answers to what happened earlier that day.
I don't have much hope without veil-thinning or the stretch drive, but Aya said I was special, so maybe...
This feels wrong, like I'm betraying Aya somehow, but I need to know.
"Meera? Can you tell me what I saw when I merged with the Parents?"
